entries.reviewSummary: Mandates maintenance of written grievance registries, date-stamping received grievances, and twenty-day response to department inquiries.

headings.title: Written registry of grievances maintained by carriers
headings.reviewNote: Directs health carriers to record all grievances, types, and outcomes in a register and provide records upon director request.

headings.title: Mandatory date stamping of received grievances
headings.reviewNote: Requires carriers to legibly and conspicuously date-stamp all grievances upon initial receipt.

headings.title: Twenty-day response deadline to department inquiries
headings.reviewNote: Requires health carriers to mail adequate specific responses to department inquiries regarding grievances within twenty days.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires filing grievance procedures and annual compliance certificates with director, and preserves enrollee judicial remedies.

headings.title: Filing grievance procedures and annual compliance certificates
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing grievance forms, procedures, and annual compliance certificates with the director subject to disapproval authority.

headings.title: Grievance description attached to plan evidence documents
headings.reviewNote: Mandates inclusion of grievance procedure descriptions in or attached to policies, certificates, and booklets given to enrollees.

headings.title: Notice of right to contact insurance department
headings.reviewNote: Requires grievance documents to state enrollee rights to contact department and provide toll-free telephone number and address.

headings.title: Preservation of legal claims and civil actions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that internal grievance procedures do not bar lawsuits in court by enrollees or defenses by health carriers.

headings.title: Judicial court judgments prevail over grievance outcomes
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that court judgments in competent jurisdictions prevail in case of conflict with internal grievance outcomes.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes two-level grievance review systems for managed care plans and sets investigative timeframes for first-level reviews.

headings.title: Establishment of two-level grievance review process
headings.reviewNote: Directs managed care plans to establish first- and second-level grievance review mechanisms for enrollees and providers.

headings.title: First-level grievance acknowledgment, investigation, and decision deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Requires written acknowledgment within ten working days, a complete investigation within twenty working days (extendable by written notice with thirty more working days), an independent decision and enrollee notice within five working days after the investigation, and notice to the submitter within fifteen working days.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs second-level grievance advisory panels, independent clinical peer reviews for adverse decisions, and appeal notifications.

headings.title: Composition of second-level grievance advisory panels
headings.reviewNote: Requires second-level review panels to include enrollees and uninvolved health carrier representatives.

headings.title: Independent clinical peer review for adverse determinations
headings.reviewNote: Requires submission to two independent clinical peers when the advisory panel preliminarily upholds an adverse determination, with the panel's decision standing if both concur, the initial adverse determination overturned if both disagree, and the panel reconvening if one disagrees (source notes: words 'heath' and 'intitial' appear in original rolls).

headings.title: Second-level review timeframes and notice of appeal rights
headings.reviewNote: Applies first-level timeframes to advisory panels and mandates written notice of rights to appeal to the director.

entries.reviewSummary: Provides for external grievance appeals to independent review organizations chosen by the director and preserves Medicaid procedures.

headings.title: External review through contracted independent review organizations
headings.reviewNote: Empowers director to resolve appealed grievances through contracted independent review organizations with binding effect and judicial review.

headings.title: Director authority regarding non-grievance general complaints
headings.reviewNote: Preserves director statutory authority to investigate and resolve consumer complaints outside formal grievance definition.

headings.title: Resolution of Medicaid grievances under program rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires grievances involving Medicaid program coverage to be resolved under established Medicaid administrative rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires expedited grievance procedures for life- or health-threatening conditions with seventy-two hour oral determination notices.

headings.title: Expedited grievance review procedures for urgent conditions
headings.reviewNote: Requires carriers to establish written procedures for expedited grievance review when standard timeframes would seriously jeopardize life, health, or ability to regain maximum function, with requests allowed orally or in writing.

headings.title: Seventy-two hour determination notice for expedited reviews
headings.reviewNote: Requires oral notice of the determination within seventy-two hours of an expedited request and written confirmation within three working days, and states sections 376.1350 to 376.1390 do not apply to health indemnity plans without a managed care component.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates standardized explanation of benefits formats for provider claim determinations and enumerates required data elements.

headings.title: Standardized explanation of benefits requirement and exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Directs health insurers to provide standardized explanation of benefits to providers and exempts limited benefit policies.

headings.title: Required contents for standardized explanation of benefits
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates nine mandatory data items on explanation of benefits including insured name, charges, denial rationale, and contacts.

headings.title: Use of standardized explanation of benefits after 2002
headings.reviewNote: Requires all health insurance carriers to use the standard explanation of benefits information after January 1, 2002.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires health care providers and carriers to utilize standardized referral documentation with specified patient and visit details.

headings.title: Standardized referral documentation requirement for providers
headings.reviewNote: Directs health care providers and health carriers conducting business in Missouri to use standardized information for referrals.

headings.title: Required items in standardized referral documents
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates eight required data items in referrals including patient details, referring and receiving providers, and visit limits.

headings.title: Use of standardized referral information after 2002
headings.reviewNote: Requires all health care providers and health carriers to use the standardized referral information after January 1, 2002.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes domestic stock life insurers to mutualize through stock acquisition plans approved by directors, stockholders, and policyholders.

headings.title: Prerequisites for mutualization plan adoption and approvals
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes conversion to mutual life insurer upon approvals by directors, outstanding stock majority, and qualifying policyholders.

headings.title: Definition of eligible policyholders for voting
headings.reviewNote: Defines policyholder qualifications for voting on mutualization plans, including individual life, pure endowments, and assignees.

headings.title: Notice and supervision of policyholders meeting
headings.reviewNote: Governs thirty-day notice, voting by mail or proxy, director appointment of election inspectors, and corporation payment of costs.

headings.title: Stock acquisition terms and director approval requirement
headings.reviewNote: Allows the plan to set the acquisition price, method, and mode of payment, requires the director's written approval of the plan and of unfixed payments, and conditions approval on remaining assets sufficient to maintain the deposit and cover liabilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes stock companies converting to mutuals to acquire and hold their own shares in trust for policyholders pending retirement.

headings.title: Acquisition of shares held in trust for policyholders
headings.reviewNote: Permits mutualizing stock life corporation to acquire its shares and assign them in trust until all stock is retired.

headings.title: Appointment and duties of stock trustees
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to appoint trustees (who must be qualified directors) and fill vacancies, sets filing, bond, expense, and removal-for-cause terms, requires dividends to be repaid to the corporation, and treats held shares as admitted assets at par value.

headings.title: Effect on existing suits, rights, contracts, and deposit
headings.reviewNote: Provides that retirement of stock and amendment of articles do not affect existing suits, rights, or contracts, and that the director retains the corporation's deposit in trust for members and policyholders.

entries.reviewSummary: Comprehensive statutory appraisal, valuation, and buyout procedure for dissenting stockholders upon company mutualization.

headings.title: Stockholder objection and demand for fair cash value
headings.reviewNote: Entitles a stockholder who files a written objection, does not vote in favor, and demands payment within twenty days after plan approval to receive fair cash value (excluding mutualization effects) within ninety days after it is agreed or determined, with conclusive presumption of consent otherwise.

headings.title: Contents of written objection and payment demand
headings.reviewNote: Requires the objection and demand to state the number and kind of shares held and the amount claimed as fair cash value.

headings.title: Cessation of dissenter appraisal right upon abandonment
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the dissenting stockholder's right to be paid fair cash value ceases when the corporation abandons the mutualization plan in accordance with this section.

headings.title: Withdrawal of payment demand requires board consent
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a stockholder's demand for fair cash value may not be withdrawn unless the corporation, by its board of directors, consents.

headings.title: Corporate response and counteroffer to dissenting stockholders
headings.reviewNote: Requires corporation to respond within ten days indicating agreement with demanded value or stating its counteroffer price.

headings.title: Agreed value, director approval, and ninety-day payment
headings.reviewNote: Provides that if value is agreed within thirty days of demand and approved by the director, payment is made within ninety days of agreement upon certificate surrender, and the shares are transferred to the trustees under section 376.143.

headings.title: Court petition to determine share fair cash value
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes stockholder or company to petition circuit court within sixty days if fair cash value is not agreed.

headings.title: Failure to petition establishes corporate counteroffer price
headings.reviewNote: Provides that failure to file valuation petition within sixty days conclusively fixes share value at amount offered by corporation.

headings.title: Required contents of valuation petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires the petition to contain a brief statement of facts, show the vote and action objected to, and state facts entitling the stockholder to the relief demanded.

headings.title: Order fixing hearing date and service of notice
headings.reviewNote: Directs court to schedule hearing on valuation petition and ensure proper advance notice to interested parties.

headings.title: Court determination of eligibility and appointment of appraisers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to determine whether the stockholder is entitled to fair cash value and for how many shares, and if so to appoint three appraisers and instruct them on their duties.

headings.title: Appraisers investigation and award filing within ten days
headings.reviewNote: Requires appraisers to report within ten days unless the court extends the time, with judgment against the corporation for the confirmed award plus interest at six percent.

headings.title: Judicial valuation upon appraisers failure to file award
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court to determine fair cash value and render judgment if appraisers fail to submit award in time.

headings.title: Simultaneous surrender of stock certificates upon payment
headings.reviewNote: Requires any judgment to provide that certificates be surrendered to the corporation simultaneously with payment, and that the judgment stands as cancellation if the holder fails to surrender them.

headings.title: Court allocation of proceeding costs as equitable
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the cost of the proceedings, including reasonable appraiser compensation fixed by the court, is assessed or apportioned as the court considers equitable.

headings.title: Special proceeding advanced on docket with civil review
headings.reviewNote: Treats the proceeding as a special proceeding advanced on the court's docket, with final orders reviewable, affirmable, modifiable, or reversible as in other civil actions.

headings.title: Joinder of dissenting stockholders in single proceeding
headings.reviewNote: Permits two or more dissenting stockholders to join as plaintiffs or be joined as defendants in one valuation action.

headings.title: Suspension of dividend rights and restoration upon abandonment
headings.reviewNote: Bars an objecting stockholder from voting shares, exercising rights, or receiving dividends unless the plan is abandoned or the demand is withdrawn with consent, credits dividends paid before abandonment, and restores stockholder status on abandonment.

headings.title: Decree ordering surrender of certificates for cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court decree ordering recalcitrant stockholders to surrender certificates, with decree standing in lieu of surrender.

headings.title: Abandonment of mutualization plan before policyholder vote
headings.reviewNote: Allows the corporation, before the policyholder vote, to abandon the plan by the same director and stockholder vote required for adoption, terminating stockholders' payment rights, with the corporation continuing as a stock life insurer.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes size, age, residency, and classification requirements for boards of directors or trustees of mutual life insurers.

headings.title: Board composition, age, and residency requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires board of three to twenty-one members, policyholder status, age eighteen or older, and at least three Missouri residents.

headings.title: Staggered board classes in articles of incorporation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes dividing board of directors into up to three staggered classes to secure organizational continuity.

headings.title: Annual election of directors in absence of classes
headings.reviewNote: Requires all directors or trustees to be elected annually unless staggered classes are established in articles.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs board of directors meeting notices, waivers of notice, and creation and authority of board executive committees.

headings.title: Notice of board meetings and waiver of notice
headings.reviewNote: Provides that board meetings follow articles notice rules and attendance waives notice unless objecting to meeting legality.

headings.title: Designation and interim authority of executive committee
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes board to designate three or more members as executive committee exercising board management authority between meetings.

headings.title: Preservation of legal board responsibility and accountability
headings.reviewNote: Provides that delegating interim management authority to executive committee does not relieve board of legal responsibilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes policyholder membership, one-vote allocation rules, board amendment powers, and assessment prohibitions for mutual insurers.

headings.title: Policyholder membership in mutual life corporation
headings.reviewNote: Requires articles of agreement to establish every policyholder as a member of the mutual life insurance corporation.

headings.title: Definition of policyholder and assignee voting eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Defines policyholder status for insureds, annuity owners, joint owners, and assignees with thirty-day recorded assignments.

headings.title: One-vote entitlement for qualifying policyholders
headings.reviewNote: Requires articles of agreement to give each policyholder insured for at least one thousand dollars (or holding an annuity requiring at least one hundred dollars annually) in force for one year only one vote regardless of policies held.

headings.title: Board authority to amend articles of agreement
headings.reviewNote: Vests power to alter or repeal articles in board of directors unless reserved to corporate members in articles.

headings.title: Articles must bar policy assessments beyond premium
headings.reviewNote: Requires a mutual legal reserve life insurer's articles to provide that it issue no life policy or annuity contract providing for any assessment beyond the regular premium.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires discount medical plan organizations to register with the director and permits authorized agents to transact business.

headings.title: Mandatory registration for discount medical plan organizations
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful to operate discount medical plan organizations without state registration or valid insurer licensing.

headings.title: Agent transaction of business for registered entities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes individuals, employees, and agents to transact discount medical plan business on behalf of registered entities.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes initial application, one-year term, annual renewal, dedicated fee deposits, and individual provider exemptions for discount plans.

headings.title: Application filing and initial registration fee
headings.reviewNote: Requires discount medical plan applicants to file approved application forms and pay two hundred fifty dollar registration fee.

headings.title: One-year registration term and expiration
headings.reviewNote: Sets discount medical plan organization registration duration at one year from registration date unless renewed.

headings.title: Annual registration renewal application and fee
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes annual one-year registration renewals upon submission of renewal application and two hundred fifty dollar fee.

headings.title: Deposit of registration fees into dedicated fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs all collected discount medical plan registration and renewal fees into the state insurance dedicated fund.

headings.title: Exemption for direct provider patient discounts
headings.reviewNote: Exempts health care providers offering direct service discounts to their own patients from organization registration rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes director examinations of discount medical plan organizations and makes nonpayment of expenses grounds for registration revocation.

headings.title: Director examination and investigation powers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to examine discount organizations, demand books and records, take sworn testimony, and assess examination expenses.

headings.title: Revocation of registration for unpaid examination costs
headings.reviewNote: Makes failure to pay incurred examination expenses grounds for denial or revocation of discount plan organization registration.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs discount medical plan processing fees, thirty-day cancellation refunds, prominent notice placement, and pro rata reimbursements.

headings.title: Authorized processing fees and periodic charge disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Permits discount organizations to charge reasonable disclosed one-time processing fees and periodic membership charges.

headings.title: Thirty-day membership cancellation right and full refund
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees full refund of periodic charges within thirty days of cancellation, adding interest if refund is delayed.

headings.title: Cancellation right set out on first page in ten-point type
headings.reviewNote: Requires the right of cancellation to be set out on the first page of the written membership materials in ten-point type or larger.

headings.title: Pro rata refund upon organization cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Requires pro rata refund of periodic charges when organization cancels membership for reasons other than nonpayment.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates bold disclosures that discount medical plans are not insurance on marketing materials, telephone sales, and membership cards.

headings.title: Mandatory written disclosures on first marketing page
headings.reviewNote: Requires twelve-point bold disclosures stating the plan is not insurance and members remain obligated to pay discounted providers.

headings.title: Oral disclosures during telephone marketing and sales
headings.reviewNote: Directs that statutory disclosures be made orally during phone solicitations and included in initial written plan materials.

headings.title: Prominent non-insurance statement on discount cards
headings.reviewNote: Requires each discount card or identifier to prominently display that this is not insurance on its front face.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires written provider agreements for discount medical plans, specifying discounted rate terms, network obligations, and record retention.

headings.title: Written agreement requirement for discount plan providers
headings.reviewNote: Requires all medical services under discount plans to be furnished pursuant to direct or network written provider agreements.

headings.title: Mandatory terms and fee schedules in agreements
headings.reviewNote: Directs provider agreements to specify discounted services, fee schedules, and commitments not to charge above discounted rates.

headings.title: Provider network agreement terms and quarterly lists
headings.reviewNote: Requires network agreements to authorize contracting and mandate quarterly updated provider rosters sent to discount organizations.

headings.title: Subcontractor compliance with network agreement requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires contracting intermediary entities to ensure provider network agreements satisfy all statutory contracting standards.

headings.title: Maintenance of active provider agreement records
headings.reviewNote: Requires discount medical plan organizations to maintain copies of all executed active health care provider agreements.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires written membership materials to include each plan benefit, the cancellation-right statement, and required disclosures, and requires forms to be submitted to the director on request (source note: both versions of this section are printed due to possible conflict).

headings.title: Required contents of written membership materials
headings.reviewNote: Mandates description of all plan benefits, cancellation rights, and statutory disclosures in member written materials.

headings.title: Submission of membership forms upon director request
headings.reviewNote: Requires discount medical plan organizations to produce all forms and written materials upon inquiry by the director.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires written membership materials to include each benefit and required disclosure, and requires forms to be filed with the director before sale, with a twenty-five-dollar fee per form (source note: both versions of this section are printed due to possible conflict).

headings.title: Comprehensive disclosures required in membership materials
headings.reviewNote: Requires written member agreements to set out every plan benefit, statutory disclosure, and member cancellation right.

headings.title: Mandatory form filing and twenty-five dollar fee
headings.reviewNote: Requires prior filing of all discount plan marketing and membership forms with unique numbers and twenty-five dollar fees.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes mandatory one hundred fifty thousand dollar minimum net worth requirements for discount medical plan organizations.

headings.title: Continuous maintenance of minimum net worth
headings.reviewNote: Requires each registered discount medical plan organization to maintain a net worth of at least one hundred fifty thousand dollars at all times (source note: word 'sections' appears twice in original rolls of S.B. 66).

headings.title: Net worth prerequisite for registration
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the director may not allow a registration unless the organization has a net worth of at least one hundred fifty thousand dollars.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires written organization approval for all marketer advertisements and executed written marketer agreements before sales activities.

headings.title: Organization approval of marketer advertising materials
headings.reviewNote: Directs that all advertisements, brochures, and cards used by marketers be approved in writing by discount organization.

headings.title: Executed written agreement required prior to marketing
headings.reviewNote: Requires executed written agreements between discount organizations and marketers prior to marketing or selling plans.

entries.reviewSummary: Enumerates grounds for registration denial or revocation, hearing rights, and immediate wind-down duties following registration surrender.

headings.title: Grounds for registration denial, suspension, or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates statutory grounds including fraud, misrepresentation, deceptive marketing, net worth failure, and statutory violations.

headings.title: Notice of suspension grounds and hearing opportunity
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice specifying statutory revocation grounds and affords opportunity for administrative hearing before director.

headings.title: Affairs wind-down upon registration surrender or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Mandates immediate wind-down of business and prohibits further advertising, fee collection, or contract renewals upon revocation.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes director administrative orders under section 374.046, license or certificate suspension or revocation for willful violations, and director civil actions under section 374.048 for discount medical plan violations, classed as level two violations.

headings.title: Director administrative orders and license action
headings.reviewNote: Allows the director to issue administrative orders under section 374.046 for violations or material aiding of violations, classifies violations as level two under section 374.049, and allows suspending or revoking a license or certificate of authority for willful violations.

headings.title: Director civil action for relief under section 374.048
headings.reviewNote: Allows the director to maintain a civil action for relief authorized under section 374.048 for violations or material aiding of violations, with violations classified as level two under section 374.049.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates mental illness coverage parity with physical health conditions, defines terms, excludes custodial care, and provides cost waivers.

headings.title: Mandatory mental health coverage parity requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires carriers to cover mental health conditions on plans on or after January 1, 2005 with no greater financial burden than for physical conditions, allows managed care delivery subject to department rules, and requires chemical dependency coverage under cited sections (source note: sections 376.825 to 376.836 were repealed by H.B. 1298 Revision, 2014).

headings.title: Statutory definitions regarding mental health conditions
headings.reviewNote: Defines chemical dependency, health benefit plan, health carrier, mental health condition, managed care organization, and rate, term, or condition for purposes of the section.

headings.title: Exemption for individual and supplemental insurance policies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts individually underwritten policies, accident-only, Medicare supplement, and long-term care plans from parity mandates.

headings.title: Mental illness coverage for state employee plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires all health insurance policies covering state employees, including the Missouri consolidated health care plan, to include coverage for mental illness, with a deferral for multiyear group policies until term expiration unless the policyholder elects earlier.

headings.title: Permitted exclusions or different limits for listed services
headings.reviewNote: States the section is not violated if an insurer applies different limits or excludes marital, family, educational, or training services unless medically necessary, school or halfway house services, custodial care, inappropriate services, or experimental treatments.

headings.title: Cost-increase waiver and administrative rulemaking standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to grant a policyholder a waiver if actual experience over any consecutive twenty-four-month period shows compliance increased premium costs by two percent, and to promulgate rules for the demonstration procedure.

entries.reviewSummary: Enforces federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act standards on health carriers, excluding supplemental and grandfathered plans.

headings.title: Definitions for federal mental health parity enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Defines health benefit plan, health carrier, and mental health condition by statutory cross-reference.

headings.title: Compliance with federal mental health parity act
headings.reviewNote: Requires health carriers covering mental conditions to comply with federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act.

headings.title: Exemptions for supplemental and pre-2014 health plans
headings.reviewNote: Excludes supplemental, Medicare supplement, short-term, and small group or individual plans purchased before 2014 from parity.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for federal parity enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Grants director authority to promulgate administrative rules to implement federal mental health parity enforcement.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates credentialing receipt notices, completed-application rules, sixty-day decisions, payments for covered services during the credentialing period, temporary coverage exemptions, prompt payment, a covered services definition, and a violation reporting mechanism.

headings.title: Two-day receipt notice and credentialing web portal
headings.reviewNote: Requires health carriers to send application receipt notices within two working days and provide status portal access.

headings.title: Incomplete application notices and ten-day supplemental requests
headings.reviewNote: Gives carriers ten days to request additional data and requires completion notice within two working days of receipt.

headings.title: Sixty-day deadline for credentialing determinations and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Mandates credentialing decisions within sixty days of complete application unless disciplinary or malpractice history exists.

headings.title: Payment for covered services during credentialing period
headings.reviewNote: Requires carriers to reimburse covered care provided during credentialing period once approved, barring balance billing of patients.

headings.title: Credentialing exemption for temporary covering practitioners
headings.reviewNote: Exempts temporary substitute practitioners covering absences up to sixty days for FMLA leave or thirty days for other reasons.

headings.title: Prompt payment law applies to eligible claims
headings.reviewNote: Provides that all claims eligible for payment under subsection 4 or 5 are subject to section 376.383.

headings.title: Definition of covered health services
headings.reviewNote: Defines covered health services as any services provided by a practitioner that would otherwise be covered if provided by a credentialed provider.

headings.title: Department mechanism for reporting violations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of commerce and insurance to establish a mechanism for reporting alleged violations of this section to the department.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines insurance policy, bars living organ donor status from being the sole factor in insurance offering, issuance, cancellation, price, conditions, or amount, directs public information, and authorizes rulemaking.

headings.title: Definition of insurance policy for living donor section
headings.reviewNote: Defines insurance policy as a life insurance contract under section 376.365, accident and sickness policy under section 376.773, or long-term care policy under section 376.1100.

headings.title: Prohibited insurance underwriting discrimination against living donors
headings.reviewNote: Provides that living organ donor status shall not be the sole factor in the offering, issuance, cancellation, price, or conditions of an insurance policy or the amount of coverage.

headings.title: Public information and donation materials on insurance access
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of commerce and insurance to provide public information on living donor access to insurance, permits both departments to make donation organization materials available, and allows gifts, grants, or donations.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Allows the director to promulgate rules to implement the section, effective only if compliant with chapter 536, with a nonseverability provision tied to the general assembly's rule review powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts qualifying faith-based health care sharing ministries from state insurance laws and mandates prominent non-insurance disclaimers.

headings.title: Exemption of health care sharing ministries from insurance
headings.reviewNote: Provides that qualifying faith-based health care sharing ministries are not insurance companies or subject to insurance laws.

headings.title: Definition and requirements of health care sharing ministry
headings.reviewNote: Defines a health care sharing ministry as a faith-based nonprofit tax-exempt organization meeting six criteria, including similar-faith membership, gifts between members, no assumption of risk, a monthly statement, and a prescribed written disclaimer.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs statutory registration of life policies and reserve security endorsements, permanent registers, and policy exemptions.

headings.title: Statutory policy registration and reserve security statement
headings.reviewNote: Permits life insurance companies to endorse policies stating net reserves are secured by pledged securities with the department.

headings.title: Maintenance of permanent policy registration register
headings.reviewNote: Requires the insurance company under director supervision to prepare and maintain a permanent register of registered policies.

headings.title: Exemptions for certain industrial, term, and group policies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts from policy registration industrial or prudential plan policies not exceeding one thousand dollars, term policies of seven years or less and ten thousand dollars or less, and group policies, while permitting registration if the company desires.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes that direct medical retainer agreements are not insurance, sets contract standards, and authorizes HSA, FSA, and HRA payments.

headings.title: Definitions of medical retainer agreement and provider
headings.reviewNote: Defines medical retainer agreement as a contract between a provider and an individual patient or legal representative for described services for an agreed fee and period, and defines provider as a licensed chiropractor, dentist, or physician.

headings.title: Medical retainer agreements excluded from insurance definition
headings.reviewNote: Provides that medical retainer agreements do not constitute the business of insurance and are not subject to chapter 376.

headings.title: No certificate of authority or license needed to sell
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a provider or agent of a provider is not required to obtain a certificate of authority or license under this section to market, sell, or offer to sell a medical retainer agreement.

headings.title: Mandatory written requirements for retainer contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires signed written agreements describing services, fees, termination rights, and prominent non-insurance disclosures.

headings.title: Retainer fee payments from health savings accounts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes paying retainer fees through health savings accounts, FSAs, HRAs, or direct employer contributions under federal law.

headings.title: Collaborative practice arrangements permitted for retainer contracts
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that providers in collaborative practice arrangements are not restricted from entering into medical retainer agreements.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts qualified membership organization self-funded health care benefit contracts from health insurance laws, with registration, sales, administrator, disclaimer, fee, marketing, and minimum coverage requirements.

headings.title: Definitions for qualified membership organization benefit contracts
headings.reviewNote: Defines contract for health care benefits, Farm Bureau, health care service, member, and qualified membership organization.

headings.title: Exemption of qualified membership contracts from insurance laws
headings.reviewNote: Excludes qualified membership self-funded health benefit contracts from state insurance laws and corporate insurance regulation.

headings.title: Five-year registration requirement and fee with director
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful to provide contracts without registration with the department, with a two-hundred-fifty-dollar application fee, five-year registration, and two-hundred-fifty-dollar renewal fee deposited in the insurance dedicated fund (source note: word 'and' appears in original rolls).

headings.title: Thirty-day membership requirement and licensed producer sales
headings.reviewNote: Requires thirty days of membership prior to benefit offers and mandates sales through licensed accident and health producers.

headings.title: Permitted administrator and claims payment standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires use of an administrator permitted under sections 376.1075 to 376.1095 and an agreement to follow benefit determination and claims payment procedures under sections 376.383, 376.690, and 376.1367.

headings.title: Reinsurance of qualified membership benefit risks
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes qualified membership organizations to reinsure self-funded health contract risks under section 375.246.

headings.title: Mandatory prominent written non-insurance disclaimer disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Requires prominent bold written notice on contracts and applications stating coverage is not insurance and lacks guaranty protection.

headings.title: Prohibition against individual post-claim medical underwriting
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits individual post-claim underwriting, rescissions, or benefit alterations while member coverage remains in effect.

headings.title: Department review of member complaints and inquiries
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of commerce and insurance, notwithstanding subsection 2, to receive and review complaints and inquiries from members pursuant to section 374.085, subject to section 374.071.

headings.title: Annual fee of one percent of Missouri claims paid
headings.reviewNote: Requires each qualified membership organization or its administrator to pay the director by March thirty-first a fee equal to one percent of Missouri claims paid in the preceding year, deposited in the insurance dedicated fund.

headings.title: No marketing of contracts as insurance
headings.reviewNote: Bars qualified membership organizations from referring to these contracts as insurance or health insurance in marketing, advertising, or public communications, and makes a violation an unlawful practice under section 407.020.

headings.title: Required essential coverage and two-million-dollar annual limit floor
headings.reviewNote: Requires contracts to include coverage for ambulatory patient services, hospitalization, emergency services, and laboratory services, and bars an annual limit of less than two million dollars per year.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines telehealth terms, bars denying coverage solely because a service is delivered by telehealth, does not require site origination fee reimbursement, sets cost-sharing parity, and preserves utilization review and provider discretion on physical presence.

headings.title: Definitions regarding telehealth services and health carriers
headings.reviewNote: Defines electronic visit, health benefit plan, health care provider, health care service, health carrier, and telehealth for purposes of the section.

headings.title: Telehealth coverage not denied if covered face-to-face
headings.reviewNote: Bars carriers and plans delivered, issued, continued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2014 from denying coverage for a service because it is provided through telehealth if the same service would be covered face-to-face.

headings.title: Denial of coverage solely for telehealth format prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits carriers from excluding services from coverage solely because they are furnished through telehealth technology.

headings.title: No requirement to reimburse originating site facility fees
headings.reviewNote: States a carrier need not reimburse a telehealth or consulting provider for site origination fees or costs, but subject to correct coding must reimburse providers for telehealth services on the same basis as in-person delivery.

headings.title: Cost-sharing parity for telehealth and in-person care
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits imposing greater deductibles, copayments, or coinsurance on telehealth services than in-person equivalents.

headings.title: Lifetime or annual dollar limit parity requirements
headings.reviewNote: Bars health carriers from establishing lifetime or annual payment maximums for telehealth that do not apply to other benefits.

headings.title: Utilization review permitted for telehealth medical necessity
headings.reviewNote: Allows carriers to undertake utilization review to determine the appropriateness of telehealth as a means of delivering a service, with determinations made in the same manner as for in-person delivery.

headings.title: Network provider limitation for covered telehealth services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes health carriers to restrict telehealth coverage to services delivered by participating in-network providers.

headings.title: Physical presence with patient not required for telehealth
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that providers are not required to be physically present with patients during covered telehealth visits.

headings.title: Exemption of supplemental and limited insurance policies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts life care, accident-only, specified disease, Medicare supplement, and long-term care policies from telehealth mandate.

entries.reviewSummary: Designated as Nora's Law, mandates coverage for remote home blood pressure monitors for pregnant and postpartum enrollees.

headings.title: Short title cited as Nora's Law
headings.reviewNote: Designates the home blood pressure monitoring statutory section as Nora's Law.

headings.title: Definitions for blood pressure monitoring coverage mandates
headings.reviewNote: Defines health benefit plan, home blood pressure monitoring device, and home blood pressure monitoring device services for purposes of the section.

headings.title: Mandatory coverage for remote blood pressure monitors
headings.reviewNote: Requires health benefit plans to cover clinical home blood pressure monitoring devices for pregnant and postpartum women.

entries.reviewSummary: Cites sections 376.2000 to 376.2014 as the Health Insurance Marketplace Innovation Act of 2013 and defines department, director, exchange, and navigator.

headings.title: Title cited as Health Insurance Marketplace Innovation Act
headings.reviewNote: Provides that sections 376.2000 to 376.2014 may be cited as the Health Insurance Marketplace Innovation Act of 2013.

headings.title: Definitions for exchange navigator regulatory provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines department, director, exchange, and navigator providing compensated enrollment services for health benefit exchanges.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires licensure for navigators, lists permitted navigator functions, bars certain producer-type activities, and sets exemptions, with a source note recording a 2016 federal preemption annotation for certain provisions.

headings.title: Navigator license required for exchange activities
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits acting as an exchange navigator or receiving navigator funding without a department navigator license.

headings.title: Permitted navigator duties and impartial assistance functions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes navigators to provide impartial exchange information, facilitate plan selection, initiate enrollment, and give referrals.

headings.title: Prohibited insurance producer and endorsement activities
headings.reviewNote: Bars unlicensed navigators from selling insurance, comparing individual plans, or advising on non-exchange products.

headings.title: Exemptions for insurance producers, attorneys, and providers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts licensed insurance producers, attorneys, and qualifying uncompensated health care providers from navigator licensing.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes navigator license qualifications, entity licenses, affiliated roster reporting, and director examination standards.

headings.title: Individual navigator application requirements and examination
headings.reviewNote: Requires age eighteen, state residence, clean disciplinary background, written examination passage, and fee payments.

headings.title: Entity navigator license application and supervision duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires entities employing or supervising navigators or receiving exchange navigator funding to obtain entity licenses.

headings.title: Director authority to verify application documentation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to demand verification documents to substantiate individual and entity navigator license applications.

headings.title: Reporting roster of affiliated individual navigators
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensed entities to maintain rosters of affiliated navigators and notify director of changes within twenty days.

headings.title: Training, continuing education, and examination standards
headings.reviewNote: Directs insurance director to establish mandatory initial training, examination, and continuing education rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes two-year navigator license terms, renewal procedures, late fees, and mandatory continuing education proof.

headings.title: Two-year duration for navigator licenses
headings.reviewNote: Sets the statutory term of individual and entity navigator licenses at two years from issuance date.

headings.title: License renewal applications and late fee assessments
headings.reviewNote: Governs license renewal filings and prescribes administrative late fees for failure to submit timely renewals.

headings.title: Continuing education compliance and license expiration
headings.reviewNote: Requires proof of required continuing education prior to renewal and provides that noncompliance causes license expiration.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes navigator license disciplinary sanctions, restitution orders, director examinations, and entity vicarious accountability.

headings.title: Administrative sanctions, license revocations, and fines
headings.reviewNote: Empowers director to suspend, revoke, refuse, or fine navigators up to one thousand dollars per violation with appeal rights.

headings.title: Restitution orders for consumer financial injury
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to order navigators to pay restitution for financial harm caused by statutory violations.

headings.title: Director power to examine affairs and records
headings.reviewNote: Grants director investigatory authority to inspect records and examine business affairs of licensed navigators.

headings.title: Entity disciplinary sanctions for unaddressed agent violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes sanctions against navigator entities if individual violations were known and not reported or corrected.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes administrative orders, civil injunctive actions, and level two penalties for navigator regulatory violations.

headings.title: Administrative enforcement orders for navigator violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director administrative orders under section 374.046 against persons committing or aiding navigator violations.

headings.title: Civil injunctive actions for navigator statutory compliance
headings.reviewNote: Empowers director to maintain civil court actions under section 374.048 to enjoin violations and obtain relief.

headings.title: Level two violation classification for navigator offenses
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violations of navigator statutory sections 376.2000 to 376.2014 as level two regulatory violations.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates reporting out-of-state administrative actions and criminal charges within thirty days, and entity termination notices.

headings.title: Thirty-day reporting of external administrative actions
headings.reviewNote: Requires navigators to report disciplinary actions in other jurisdictions or agencies within thirty days of final disposition.

headings.title: Thirty-day reporting of criminal prosecutions
headings.reviewNote: Requires navigators to report criminal prosecutions in any jurisdiction within thirty days of initial pretrial hearings.

headings.title: Twenty-day notification of navigator employee terminations
headings.reviewNote: Requires entities to report termination of navigators for cause within twenty days and furnish supporting records upon request.

entries.reviewSummary: Applies insurance statutes to navigators, establishes statutory severability, and authorizes director administrative rulemaking.

headings.title: Insurance code applicability to exchange navigators
headings.reviewNote: Applies insurance regulatory chapters and deems navigator activities to constitute transacting insurance business.

headings.title: Severability of navigator statutory provisions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that invalid applications or sections do not impair remaining valid provisions of navigator statutes.

headings.title: Director rulemaking authority and nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to promulgate rules subject to chapter 536 and nonseverability conditions.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines terms and declares unenforceable certain carrier-provider contract provisions restricting disclosure of contractual payment amounts that would prevent determining out-of-pocket cost, with a source note recording an effective date of 10-14-16 after a veto override.

headings.title: Definitions regarding contractual payment disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Defines contractual payment amount, enrollee, health care provider, health care service, and health carrier.

headings.title: Gag clauses on payment disclosures unenforceable
headings.reviewNote: Declares contract clauses restricting provider disclosure of allowable payment amounts or out-of-pocket costs unenforceable.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires access to a step therapy override exception process, grounds for granting overrides, carrier authority to request documentation, authorization upon granting, and preservation of generic or alternative drug requirements.

headings.title: Step therapy override exception request procedures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes prescribing providers and patients to request step therapy overrides through clear and accessible processes.

headings.title: Required grounds for granting step therapy override
headings.reviewNote: Requires granting an override if the patient tried the required drugs under current or previous coverage and discontinued them for lack of efficacy, diminished effect, or adverse event, or the treating provider attests the drug is necessary to save the patient's life; samples are not a trial.

headings.title: Carrier may request supporting documentation
headings.reviewNote: Allows the carrier, plan, or utilization review organization to request relevant documentation from the patient or provider to support the override exception request.

headings.title: Immediate authorization upon granting exception request
headings.reviewNote: Requires the carrier, plan, or utilization review organization, upon granting an override, to authorize dispensation and coverage of the prescribed drug if it is a covered drug under the policy or contract.

headings.title: Generic or alternative drug requirements and prescribing preserved
headings.reviewNote: States the section does not prevent a carrier, plan, or review organization from requiring a patient to try a generic equivalent or other brand name drug first, or a provider from prescribing a drug it determines medically appropriate.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires life insurers to perform periodic death master file comparisons, locate beneficiaries, and escheat unclaimed proceeds.

headings.title: Semi-annual death master file comparison requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers to compare in-force life policies, contracts, and retained asset accounts against a death master file at least semiannually, and within ninety days of a match to confirm death, determine benefits, locate beneficiaries, and provide claims forms.

headings.title: Use of electronic or most accessible records for comparison
headings.reviewNote: Requires the comparison to use electronic records where available and otherwise the records most easily accessible by the insurer.

headings.title: Policy may be considered in force if death unconfirmed
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an insurer unable to confirm death after a match and the required good-faith efforts may consider the policy, contract, or account to be in force according to its terms.

headings.title: Group life insurance recordkeeping service prerequisite
headings.reviewNote: Limits group life death confirmation duties to contracts where insurer agreed to provide administrative record-keeping.

headings.title: Authorized disclosure of necessary locator information
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes disclosure of minimum necessary personal data to persons who can assist in locating missing beneficiaries.

headings.title: Fees for death master searches prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers or third parties from charging beneficiaries any fees for death master file searches or verifications.

headings.title: Payment of benefits and escheat of unclaimed proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Makes benefits plus accrued contractual interest payable first to designated beneficiaries or owners, or escheat to the state as unclaimed property under section 447.510 if they cannot be found.

headings.title: Director rulemaking authority and nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to adopt administrative rules to enforce death master file comparison statutory provisions.

headings.title: Violations as unfair trade practices and private actions
headings.reviewNote: Classifies business practice violations as unfair trade practices while stating section implies no private cause of action.

headings.title: Preservation of policy claims compliance provisions
headings.reviewNote: Preserves insurer right to require compliance with contract terms regarding filing and proof of claims.

headings.title: Director exemption for documented insurer undue hardship
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to exempt insurers from comparison duties upon demonstrating compliance would cause undue hardship.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines funding agreements, non-security classification, life insurer issuance authority, and director rulemaking powers.

headings.title: Definition and non-security status of funding agreements
headings.reviewNote: Defines funding agreement as contract to accumulate funds without mortality contingencies and excludes it from securities.

headings.title: Authority of life insurers to issue funding agreements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes life insurance companies to issue funding agreements and deems issuance doing insurance business.

headings.title: Director rulemaking authority for funding agreement implementation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to promulgate implementation rules subject to chapter 536 and nonseverability conditions.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes six hundred thousand dollar capital and surplus minimums for life insurers, grandfathering, and license revocations.

headings.title: Minimum capital and surplus for stock life insurers
headings.reviewNote: Requires six hundred thousand dollars capital and equal surplus invested in statutory securities prior to business commencement.

headings.title: Ongoing maintenance of required capital and surplus
headings.reviewNote: Requires stock life companies to maintain initial capital and surplus levels continuously to write new business.

headings.title: Temporary grandfathering provisions for 1982 licensees
headings.reviewNote: Provides temporary grandfathering license renewals through 1984 for stock companies maintaining nine hundred thousand dollars.

headings.title: Formation requirements for mutual life insurance companies
headings.reviewNote: Bars a mutual company from commencing or continuing business until written agreements for assurance by at least one hundred persons, at least six hundred thousand dollars in cash premiums, and six hundred thousand dollars surplus exist, while permitting compliance with sections 362.180 to 362.195.

headings.title: Mutual company renewal grandfathering through 1984
headings.reviewNote: Allows a mutual company licensed on August 13, 1982 to renew its license until December 31, 1984 by maintaining at least nine hundred thousand dollars in paid-in premiums in lieu of the surplus requirement.

headings.title: Revocation of certificate of authority for violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to revoke certificate of authority for violation of capital and surplus statutory requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes permissible insurer investments, admitted asset standards, and mandatory written board-approved investment plans.

headings.title: Permissible investments and admitted asset criteria
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes investments conforming to chapter 376 and requires income-producing or derivative eligibility for admitted asset status.

headings.title: Written investment plan approved by board of directors
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to adopt a written investment plan (within three months after August 28, 2007), supervise investments, evidence annual review by resolution, review reports at least quarterly, and act with prudent care.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits certain insurer investments and guarantees involving officers, directors, and their entities, evasion transactions, general partnerships, and own-stock loans, with an exception allowing affiliates to be general partners.

headings.title: Prohibited officer investments, evasion, partnerships, and own-stock loans
headings.reviewNote: Bars insurers from investments or guarantees for officers, directors, or their ten-percent-owned entities (except as allowed), evasion transactions, general partner investments (with exceptions), and investing or lending on the security of their own stock.

headings.title: Affiliates not barred from becoming general partners
headings.reviewNote: States that the general partner prohibition in subdivision (4) of subsection 1 does not prohibit a subsidiary or other affiliate of the insurer from becoming a general partner.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires director written approval for insurer loans, guarantees, and property agreements involving officers, directors, or their interested persons, and lists loans and advances allowed without prior approval.

headings.title: Officer and director transactions requiring director approval
headings.reviewNote: Bars an insurer, without the director's written approval, from loans or investments in, guarantees for, or property purchase or sale agreements with officers, directors, or persons in which they have a financial interest, subject to listed exceptions.

headings.title: Loans and advances allowed without director approval
headings.reviewNote: Allows without prior approval policy loans, expense advances to officers or directors, certain relocation loans secured by residences, and certain regulated noninsurance subsidiary loans and advances on specified terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Imposes portfolio diversification caps: three percent per issuer, twenty percent in medium/lower grade debt, and Canadian limits.

headings.title: Issuer concentration limits for admitted assets
headings.reviewNote: Limits single-person investments to three percent of admitted assets and five percent in depository voting securities.

headings.title: Aggregate limits on medium and lower grade investments
headings.reviewNote: Caps medium and lower grade debt at twenty percent and lower grade at ten percent of admitted assets.

headings.title: Portfolio limits on Canadian investment holdings
headings.reviewNote: Limits Canadian investments to forty percent of admitted assets with adjustments for Canadian business liabilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes investments in rated government bonds, Canadian debt, mutual funds, state obligations, and rated corporate instruments.

headings.title: Acquisition of United States government credit instruments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes acquiring rated credit instruments issued or guaranteed by the United States or federal enterprises.

headings.title: Acquisition of Canadian government credit instruments
headings.reviewNote: Permits acquiring rated credit instruments of Canada or qualifying Canadian government-sponsored enterprises up to forty percent of admitted assets (source note: words 'subdivision (6)' appear in original rolls).

headings.title: Money market funds and state general obligation bonds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rated money market mutual funds, state general obligations, and multilateral development banks up to ten percent.

headings.title: Preferred stocks meeting rated credit standards
headings.reviewNote: Permits preferred stock investments up to twenty percent of admitted assets, capping lower-rated preferreds at ten percent.

headings.title: Acquisition of other rated credit instruments not foreign
headings.reviewNote: Allows acquiring, in addition to instruments eligible under subsections 1 to 4, rated credit instruments that are not foreign investments, subject to subsection 6 and section 376.297.

headings.title: Five percent portfolio cap on special rated instruments
headings.reviewNote: Caps special rated credit instruments at five percent of admitted assets unless specifically exempted by rule.

entries.reviewSummary: Permits equity interests in business entities organized in domestic jurisdictions, sets aggregate and unlisted-equity caps, excludes investments available under section 376.302, and restricts short sales.

headings.title: Permitted equity interests in business entities
headings.reviewNote: Allows an insurer, subject to section 376.297, to acquire equity interests in business entities organized under the laws of any domestic jurisdiction.

headings.title: Twenty percent aggregate cap and five percent unlisted equity cap
headings.reviewNote: Bars acquisitions that would put aggregate holdings under this section above twenty percent of admitted assets, or, except for mutual funds, unlisted equity interests above five percent of admitted assets.

headings.title: Exclusion of mortgage and real estate investments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits acquiring under equity rules investments eligible under mortgage or real estate investment provisions.

headings.title: Restrictions on short sales of equity interests
headings.reviewNote: Bars short selling equity interests unless the insurer owns the interest or an unrestricted right to it exercisable within six months of the short sale.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes investments in income-producing tangible personal property and equipment leases, setting valuation and portfolio limits.

headings.title: Acquisition of tangible personal property and equipment trusts
headings.reviewNote: Allows acquiring tangible personal property or equity interests in it, directly or through listed vehicles, if subject to a lease with a person whose rated credit instruments meet section 376.298 standards and payments return the insurer's cost plus an adequate return.

headings.title: Computation of investment amount net of nonrecourse borrowing
headings.reviewNote: Requires computing each investment on the out-of-pocket purchase price and related expenses, net of nonrecourse borrowing to finance the purchase price.

headings.title: Two percent aggregate and one-half percent per item limits
headings.reviewNote: Bars acquisitions that would put aggregate holdings under this section above two percent of admitted assets, or above one-half of one percent of admitted assets for any single item of tangible personal property.

headings.title: Aggregation of investments for issuer diversification limits
headings.reviewNote: Requires aggregating personal property lease investments with issuer obligations for diversification limits.

headings.title: Exemption for affiliate cost-sharing lease arrangements
headings.reviewNote: States the section does not apply to tangible personal property lease arrangements between an insurer and its subsidiaries and affiliates under a cost-sharing arrangement permitted under chapter 382.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs real estate mortgages, direct real estate investments, income-producing properties, and principal office facilities.

headings.title: Mortgage loans and commercial real estate obligations
headings.reviewNote: Allows acquiring obligations secured by domestic real estate mortgages subject to loan-to-value limits (ninety, eighty, or seventy-five percent), second mortgage limits, restructured loan treatment, and an exemption for qualifying credit lease transactions.

headings.title: Direct acquisition and management of income-producing properties
headings.reviewNote: Allows an insurer to acquire, manage, and dispose of income-producing domestic real estate (including real estate intended for development as an existing program), with nonrecourse encumbrances deducted for limit calculations.

headings.title: Real estate for company office accommodation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes acquiring real estate for home office accommodation and convenient corporate transaction of business.

headings.title: Percentage limits on mortgage and real estate investments
headings.reviewNote: Sets admitted-asset limits for mortgage loans, construction loans, real estate parcels, and aggregate mortgage and real estate holdings, with a conditional residential mortgage increase and a ten percent limit on real estate under subsection 3 (source printing of subdivision (1) reads 'would not exceed').

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes foreign investments, foreign currency denominated instruments, currency hedging, and foreign jurisdiction caps.

headings.title: Acquisition of foreign investments and sovereign debt caps
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes foreign investments up to twenty percent of admitted assets, capping single countries at ten or three percent.

headings.title: Foreign currency denominated investments and currency exposure
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes foreign currency investments up to ten percent of assets, subject to sovereign credit ratings.

headings.title: Hedging contracts insulating against currency fluctuations
headings.reviewNote: Provides that foreign investments hedged into United States currency under section 375.345 are not deemed foreign currency.

headings.title: Authorized foreign insurers investments in host countries
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurers doing business abroad to invest in foreign jurisdictions to meet foreign regulatory reserves.

headings.title: Unauthorized insurers with foreign risks investments
headings.reviewNote: Permits insurers with foreign risks to invest in foreign currency instruments up to 105 percent of foreign reserves.

headings.title: Aggregation of foreign investments with domestic types
headings.reviewNote: Requires foreign investments to be aggregated with domestic assets of the same type for chapter compliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes leeway investment authority allowing insurers to invest up to ten percent of assets outside statutory caps.

headings.title: Leeway authority for investments exceeding specific statutory limits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes investments exceeding specific statutory quantitative caps up to three percent of total admitted assets.

headings.title: General leeway investment basket up to ten percent
headings.reviewNote: Allows acquiring investments of any kind not specifically prohibited by the chapter without regard to sections 376.297 to 376.304 limits, up to the lesser of ten percent of admitted assets or seventy-five percent of capital and surplus, with a three percent limit per person.

headings.title: Additional leeway investments subject to prior director approval
headings.reviewNote: Allows additional investments not specifically prohibited with the director's prior approval and a prudence showing, up to the greater of twenty-five percent of capital and surplus or one hundred percent of capital and surplus less ten percent of admitted assets.

headings.title: Prohibited transactions and derivative trading excluded from leeway
headings.reviewNote: Bars acquiring prohibited assets under section 376.294 or derivative instruments under leeway basket authority.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs life insurer separate accounts, including establishment by board resolution, special voting rights, investment freedom and transfer limits, valuation, director regulation and qualification of variable contracts, contract statements, and applicable insurance laws.

headings.title: Definition and asset insulation of separate accounts
headings.reviewNote: Defines separate account and provides that allocated assets and liabilities are insulated from general corporate debts.

headings.title: Establishment of separate accounts by board resolution
headings.reviewNote: Allows a domestic life insurer, after board resolution, to establish separate accounts and allocate amounts to them under individual or group contracts providing fixed or variable benefits.

headings.title: Establishment of variable voting and management control rights
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurers to grant special voting and governance rights to separate account contract holders under federal law.

headings.title: Investment freedom and limits on transfers between accounts
headings.reviewNote: Allows separate account amounts to be invested without regard to general life insurer investment laws, except assets at least equal to guaranteed reserve liability, and restricts transfers between separate and general accounts absent cash, director approval, or equivalent value.

headings.title: Valuation of separate account assets
headings.reviewNote: Requires assets allocated to a separate account to be valued at market value, or as provided by contract or written rules if no market exists, with guaranteed-benefit portions valued under the company's general asset rules, unless the director approves otherwise.

headings.title: Director regulatory authority over variable contracts
headings.reviewNote: Gives the director sole and exclusive authority to regulate issuance and sale of separate account contracts and issue rules and licensing requirements, exempts issuers from securities registration, and permits consultation with the commissioner of securities.

headings.title: Director qualification review before contract delivery
headings.reviewNote: Bars delivery of separate account contracts in this state until the company satisfies the director its operations will not be hazardous, with the director considering history, financial condition, officer fitness, and foreign jurisdiction protections.

headings.title: Affiliated or subsidiary company may satisfy qualification
headings.reviewNote: Allows a subsidiary or affiliated authorized life insurer to be deemed to meet subsection 7 if either it or the parent or affiliate meets the requirements.

headings.title: Required statements in variable benefit contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires contracts paying variable benefits to state how variable dollar benefits are determined, state that amounts may decrease or increase, and state on the first page that benefits are on a variable basis.

headings.title: Insurance laws apply to separate accounts
headings.reviewNote: Provides that, except as otherwise provided in the section, all pertinent insurance laws of this state apply to separate accounts and related contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs investment pools for affiliated insurers, qualification standards, management agreements, and holding company disclosures.

headings.title: Investment of capital reserve and surplus in investment pools
headings.reviewNote: Allows the capital reserve and surplus of life insurers to be invested in an investment pool meeting the section's requirements, in addition to other permitted investments.

headings.title: Definitions of business entity and qualified bank
headings.reviewNote: Defines business entity and qualified bank for purposes of the investment pool section.

headings.title: Pool investment limits, manager, custody, and pooling agreement terms
headings.reviewNote: Limits pool investments to thirty percent of an insurer's assets, restricts pool activities, sets manager qualifications, record and custody requirements, and requires a written pooling agreement covering ownership, withdrawals, distributions, and director inspection.

headings.title: Prior approval of pooling agreement and annual reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires the pooling agreement and related arrangements to be submitted for prior approval under section 382.195, excludes ordinary-course pool transactions from section 382.195, and requires annual reporting in the section 382.100 registration statement.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates admission of willing licensed physicians into closed provider networks at a fifteen percent discount from standard fee schedules.

headings.title: Mandatory network admission for discounted willing physicians
headings.reviewNote: Requires closed health carrier networks to admit licensed physicians agreeing to fees fifteen percent below standard rates.

headings.title: Prerequisite provider credentialing and standard contract criteria
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the section does not apply to a physician who does not meet the carrier's selection standards and credentialing criteria or has not entered the carrier's standard participating provider agreement.

headings.title: Definitions of health carrier, physician, and closed network
headings.reviewNote: Defines health carrier, licensed physician, and closed exclusive provider network for network participation rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires life assurance companies to file annual sworn financial statements with the director and protects officer compensation confidentiality.

headings.title: Annual sworn statement within sixty days after January first
headings.reviewNote: Directs life assurance company officers to prepare under oath and deposit with the director, annually on January first or within sixty days thereafter, a statement for the preceding calendar year covering policies, premiums, losses, expenses, assets, liabilities, dividends, and other required facts.

headings.title: Confidentiality of employee and officer compensation records
headings.reviewNote: Provides that employee and executive compensation information in annual statements is exempt from public disclosure.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates annual ascertainment and apportionment of surplus to participating policies, dividend payment and option rules, participation rights in policies, and contracts not required to receive dividends.

headings.title: Annual ascertainment and distribution of earned surplus
headings.reviewNote: Requires domestic life insurers to calculate and distribute earned surplus on participating policies annually starting year three.

headings.title: Permitted contingency surplus reserves before dividend allocation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retaining contingency surplus up to greater of five hundred thousand dollars or ten percent of policy reserves.

headings.title: Policy anniversary dividend payment and premium condition
headings.reviewNote: Directs that dividends be payable on policy anniversaries conditioned only on completion of current year premiums.

headings.title: Dividend payment options and default policy selection
headings.reviewNote: Provides dividend options of cash, premium payment, accumulation at interest, or paid-up addition if the policy so provides, with the policy-stated option effective if the owner does not elect within a policy-allowed period of at least thirty-one days.

headings.title: Dividends on term insurance and pure endowment contracts
headings.reviewNote: Governs dividend options applicable to extended term insurance, individual participating term policies, and annuities.

headings.title: Participating policies must carry right to share surplus
headings.reviewNote: Bars stock or mutual life insurers from issuing, on or after January 1, 1946, participating policies or contracts that do not by their terms give the right to participate in divisible surplus earnings.

headings.title: Additional interest permitted and participating classification
headings.reviewNote: Allows participating and nonparticipating policies to provide additional declared interest on deferred proceeds without making a nonparticipating policy participating, and deems policies with surplus-participation provisions participating, with an exception for exchangeable nonparticipating policies.

headings.title: Contracts not required to receive dividends
headings.reviewNote: States the section does not require dividends on immediate annuities, deferred annuities after deferment, accident or health policies, default-triggered extended term, pure endowment, or paid-up insurance, paid-up additions, or reinsurance agreements.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Standard Valuation Law and defines key actuarial, principle-based, valuation manual, and NAIC terminology.
