headings.title: Short title cited as Standard Valuation Law
headings.reviewNote: Cites sections 376.365 to 376.380 as the Standard Valuation Law.

headings.title: Definitions for standard valuation manual and reserves
headings.reviewNote: Defines accident and health insurance, appointed actuary, NAIC, principle-based valuation, and valuation manual.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates annual director valuation of life, annuity, and health reserves, recognizes foreign valuations, and governs pre-1993 policies.

headings.title: Director annual valuation of reserve liabilities
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to annually value or cause to be valued reserves for life insurance policies and annuity and pure endowment contracts issued on or after the section 376.670 operative date and before the valuation manual operative date, with acceptance of other jurisdictions' valuations for foreign or alien companies.

headings.title: Annual valuation of contracts issued on or after valuation manual date
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to annually value reserves for life, annuity, pure endowment, accident and health, and deposit-type contracts issued on or after the valuation manual operative date, and allows accepting another jurisdiction's compliant valuation for foreign or alien companies.

headings.title: Optional calculation standards for pre-1993 policies
headings.reviewNote: Permits companies to calculate reserves on policies issued before August 28, 1993, or on director-established categories issued after, under any standards producing greater aggregate reserves, and to adopt lower standards with director approval but not below the minimum.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires carriers to offer medication synchronization services, bars charging more than the applicable co-payment for synchronized partial fills, and requires a full dispensing fee, with source notes recording effective dates and a veto override.

headings.title: Mandatory offer of medication synchronization services
headings.reviewNote: Requires health benefit plans providing prescription coverage to offer medication synchronization for chronic condition drugs.

headings.title: Co-payment cap on partial fills and full dispensing fee
headings.reviewNote: Requires carriers under medication synchronization services not to charge more than the otherwise applicable co-payment for a participating provider's partial-quantity dispensing and to pay the pharmacy a full dispensing fee.

headings.title: Definitions by reference to section 376.1350
headings.reviewNote: Gives health carrier, managed care plan, health benefit plan, enrollee, and participating provider the same meanings as in section 376.1350.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes legal minimum standards for policy valuation, statutory interest rates, principle-based reserves, and data confidentiality.

headings.title: Minimum reserve standards for life and annuity contracts
headings.reviewNote: Establishes minimum reserve valuation tables, Commissioners reserve valuation method, and net premium standards.

headings.title: Statutory valuation interest rate formulas and determination
headings.reviewNote: Defines statutory valuation interest rates based on Moody's corporate bond averages for various life and annuity guarantees.

headings.title: Minimum reserve standards for accident and health insurance
headings.reviewNote: Applies valuation manual standards to accident and health contracts issued on or after manual operative date.

headings.title: Actuarial opinions of reserves prior to valuation manual
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual actuarial opinions on reserve adequacy submitted by qualified actuaries prior to valuation manual operative date.

headings.title: Actuarial opinions and asset adequacy analysis after manual
headings.reviewNote: Mandates annual opinions of appointed actuaries regarding reserve adequacy and asset support under valuation manual.

headings.title: Prescribed valuation manual standards for post-operative policies
headings.reviewNote: Makes the valuation manual standard the minimum for policies issued on or after the manual's operative date, defines that date and manual change effectiveness, sets required manual contents, and gives the director actuarial examination and assumption-change powers.

headings.title: Mandatory requirements for principle-based reserve valuations
headings.reviewNote: Requires principle-based valuations to quantify material risks, incorporate margins, and maintain comprehensive oversight governance.

headings.title: Submission of experience data for statistical analysis
headings.reviewNote: Requires a company, for policies in force on or after the valuation manual's operative date, to submit mortality, morbidity, policyholder behavior, or expense experience and other data as the manual prescribes.

headings.title: Confidentiality protections for actuarial memorandums and data
headings.reviewNote: Protects principle-based valuation reports and actuarial memorandums as confidential privileged regulatory materials.

headings.title: Director exemption of domestic Missouri-only product forms
headings.reviewNote: Allows the director to exempt specific product forms or lines of a domestic company licensed and doing business only in Missouri from subsection 6 by written exemption, if reserves use pre-manual assumptions and methods plus any regulatory requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs prompt payment of health care claims, including definitions, forty-eight hour receipt acknowledgment, processing-day deadlines, interest and penalties, denial monitoring, fraud notice, specific denial reasons, and requests for additional information.

headings.title: Definitions for prompt claim payment and processing
headings.reviewNote: Defines claimant, clean claim, denial, health care provider, health carrier, processing days, and additional information.

headings.title: Forty-eight hour electronic acknowledgment of claim receipt
headings.reviewNote: Requires health carriers to send electronic acknowledgments of claim receipt within forty-eight hours of submission.

headings.title: Thirty-day claim status notice and payment timeline
headings.reviewNote: Requires a carrier, within thirty processing days after receipt, to send an electronic or facsimile status notice stating whether the claim is clean or needs additional information, with pay-or-deny for clean claims and a request for information otherwise.

headings.title: Ten-day determination deadline following receipt of info
headings.reviewNote: Directs carriers to pay undisputed portions, deny claims, or make final information requests within ten days of receiving data.

headings.title: Five-day final determination following final information response
headings.reviewNote: Requires health carriers to pay or deny claims within five processing days of receiving requested supplemental data.

headings.title: Interest and daily penalty assessments on unpaid claims
headings.reviewNote: Imposes one percent monthly interest and one percent daily penalties on claims unpaid after forty-five processing days.

headings.title: Department monitoring of claim denials
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of commerce and insurance to monitor denials and determine whether the health carrier acted reasonably.

headings.title: Notice to department of suspected fraudulent claims
headings.reviewNote: Requires a carrier or third-party contractor with reasonable grounds to believe a fraudulent claim is being made to notify the department pursuant to sections 375.991 to 375.994.

headings.title: Denial must state specific reason
headings.reviewNote: Requires denial of a claim to be communicated to the claimant with the specific reason, and provides that a claim without a communicated specific reason is not considered denied under sections 376.383 or 376.384.

headings.title: Requirements for requests for additional information
headings.reviewNote: Requires requests to specify all documentation needed to process the claim as clean, to be reasonable and pertain solely to the carrier's liability, and requires acknowledging receipt within five calendar days or paying the claim.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets claim filing windows, refund limits, electronic claim format standards, department compliance monitoring and penalties, waivers, provider complaint methods, medical code sets, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Claim filing windows, refund limits, and electronic receipt confirmation
headings.reviewNote: Requires carriers to permit nonparticipating providers up to one year and participating providers up to six months (unless the contract differs) to file claims, bars refund or offset requests more than twelve months after payment except for fraud or misrepresentation, and requires confirmation of electronic claim receipt within one working day.

headings.title: Mandatory electronic claim submission standards by providers
headings.reviewNote: Requires claims on or after January 1, 2003 to be submitted electronically consistent with federal HIPAA administrative simplification standards, exempts nonelectronic claims from section 376.383, and requires carriers to provide readily accessible electronic filing.

headings.title: Director monitoring and auditing of carrier claim practices
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to monitor carrier compliance beginning January 1, 2002, defines compliance as properly processing ninety-five percent of claims, and allows administrative penalties up to twenty-five dollars per noncompliant claim with an annual cap of two hundred fifty thousand dollars (source note: word 'it' appears in original rolls).

headings.title: Director order to remit interest and penalty
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director, upon finding carriers failing to pay required interest, to order payment of the interest and assess a monetary penalty payable to the state of up to twenty-five percent of the unpaid interest.

headings.title: Carrier waiver request for act of God or good cause
headings.reviewNote: Allows a carrier to request a waiver of the requirements of this section and section 376.383 if based on an act of God or other good cause as determined by the director.

headings.title: Department provider complaint mechanism for claim delays
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to develop a method for provider complaints about violations, requires providers to first contact the carrier about claim status, and lists information complaints should contain.

headings.title: Uniform electronic claim format and standard medical code sets
headings.reviewNote: Requires electronically submitted claims on or after January 1, 2003 to use a uniform format with standard medical code sets promulgated by department rules consistent with but no more stringent than federal HIPAA standards.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority for prompt claim enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department of commerce and insurance to promulgate rules implementing claim reimbursement statutes.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires covered entities to offer coverage for physician-prescribed diabetes equipment, supplies, and self-management training, with cost-sharing parity, no reduction of other coverage, and exemptions.

headings.title: Offer of coverage for diabetes equipment, supplies, and training
headings.reviewNote: Requires specified entities to offer coverage for physician-prescribed medically appropriate and necessary equipment, supplies, and self-management training for diabetes, covering gestational, type I, and type II diabetes.

headings.title: Cost-sharing parity for diabetes supplies and services
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits imposing greater deductibles or copayments on diabetes supplies and education than other general medical care.

headings.title: Prohibition on reducing other plan health benefits
headings.reviewNote: Bars health insurance issuers from reducing or eliminating other covered health benefits to offset diabetes coverage costs.

headings.title: Exemptions for supplemental and limited benefit policies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts accident-only, specified disease, hospital indemnity, Medicare supplement, and long-term care plans from mandate.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines terms, bars pharmacy benefits manager contract provisions requiring point-of-sale payments above the lesser of copayment or cash price, protects pharmacist cost information, bars charging unknown fees, and provides exemptions, notice, and enforcement.

headings.title: Definitions for pharmacy benefits manager restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Defines covered person, health benefit plan, pharmacy, pharmacist, and pharmacy benefits manager.

headings.title: Point-of-sale payment limited to lesser of copayment or cash price
headings.reviewNote: Bars a pharmacy benefits manager from including in contracts entered or modified on or after August 28, 2018 a provision requiring a covered person to pay at point of sale more than the lesser of the plan copayment or the cash price.

headings.title: Pharmacist right to inform patients of cash options
headings.reviewNote: Protects right of pharmacists to inform covered patients regarding copayment amounts and lower-cost options.

headings.title: Fees unknown at claim adjudication prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Bars a pharmacy benefits manager from charging or holding a pharmacist or pharmacy responsible for any fee amount related to a claim not known at adjudication, unless it results from improperly paid claims or charges for administering a health benefit plan.

headings.title: Exemption for Medicare Part D and federal plans
headings.reviewNote: Exempts Medicare Part D claims and federally regulated programs from state PBM contractual restriction statutes.

headings.title: Written notice to carriers of conflicts of interest
headings.reviewNote: Requires a pharmacy benefits manager to notify in writing any contracting carrier if it has a conflict of interest, commonality of ownership, or other relationship with any other carrier it contracts with.

headings.title: Department enforcement authority over pharmacy benefit managers
headings.reviewNote: Directs department of commerce and insurance to enforce statutory limitations and restrictions on PBMs.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates pharmacy benefits manager maximum allowable cost pricing, seven-day update cycles, fourteen-day appeal procedures, and appeal outcomes, with source notes recording effective dates and a veto override.

headings.title: Definitions regarding maximum allowable cost drug pricing
headings.reviewNote: Defines contracted pharmacy, health carrier, maximum allowable cost, MAC list, pharmacy, and pharmacy benefits manager.

headings.title: Seven-day update cycle for maximum allowable cost lists
headings.reviewNote: Requires PBM contracts to identify pricing sources and update MAC pricing and product lists at least every seven days.

headings.title: Mandatory reimbursement based on updated market pricing
headings.reviewNote: Directs PBMs to reimburse pharmacies using MAC prices updated to reflect wholesale marketplace prices every seven days.

headings.title: Prerequisite generic drug availability for MAC listing
headings.reviewNote: Bars placing a drug on a maximum allowable cost list unless at least two therapeutically equivalent multisource generic drugs, or at least one generic drug from at least one manufacturer, are generally available to network pharmacies from national or regional wholesalers.

headings.title: Fourteen-day internal pricing dispute appeal process
headings.reviewNote: Requires contracts to include a fourteen-day MAC appeal window and mandates PBM resolution within fourteen days of receipt.

headings.title: Required NDC identification for denied pricing appeals
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that denied MAC appeals provide specific denial reasons and national drug codes of available cheaper products.

headings.title: Price adjustments and rebilling for successful pricing appeals
headings.reviewNote: Requires a pharmacy benefits manager, on a successful appeal, to adjust the maximum allowable cost price effective the day after the decision, apply it to similarly situated pharmacies as it determines, and allow the successful pharmacy to reverse and rebill the claim.

headings.title: Grounds on which pricing appeals shall be upheld
headings.reviewNote: Requires appeals to be upheld if the pharmacy was not reimbursed at pricing updated as required under subsection 3, or the drug does not meet the subsection 4 requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires pharmacy benefits managers to obtain department licenses and establishes disciplinary grounds and administrative hearing procedures.

headings.title: Definitions of health carrier and PBM terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines health carrier and pharmacy benefits manager by cross-reference to sections 376.1350 and 376.388.

headings.title: Mandatory department licensure for pharmacy benefits managers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits entities from acting as pharmacy benefits managers without obtaining a license from insurance department.

headings.title: Disciplinary proceedings before administrative hearing commission
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to file an administrative hearing commission complaint under chapter 621 against a licensee on listed grounds, with censure, probation up to five years, suspension up to three years, or revocation (source note: word 'benefit' appears in original rolls).

entries.reviewSummary: Requires group health policies to provide individual conversion rights upon termination without proof of insurability, setting terms.

headings.title: Mandatory converted policy upon group coverage termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires group policies to offer converted individual policies without insurability proof upon employee termination, setting conditions.

headings.title: Alternative conversion plans and service-basis policies
headings.reviewNote: Allows an insurer to offer alternative conversion plans or service-basis converted policies the director finds satisfy the intent of the sections, and allows a health service corporation to limit conversion offerings to one plan.

headings.title: Notice of conversion privilege in certificates
headings.reviewNote: Requires notification of the conversion privilege to be included in each certificate of coverage.

headings.title: Converted policy effective day after group termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires all converted policies to become effective on the day immediately following the date insurance under the group policy terminates.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs policy conversion rights for retiring employees, eligible dependents, and family members losing group health insurance coverage.

headings.title: Conversion rights for retiring employees and dependents
headings.reviewNote: Allows an employee whose group coverage would continue after retirement but before Medicare eligibility to elect the same conversion rights as on termination, and allows the converted policy to reduce or end coverage upon Medicare or similar eligibility.

headings.title: Conversion rights for surviving spouses, spouses, and children
headings.reviewNote: Extends the conversion privilege to a surviving spouse and children on the employee's death, to a spouse whose coverage ends while the employee remains insured, and to a child ceasing to be a qualified family member, subject to this section and section 376.397.

entries.reviewSummary: Allows converted policy benefit parity with underlying group policies, group coverage in lieu of conversion, and out-of-state forms.

headings.title: Benefit level options matching underlying group policies
headings.reviewNote: Allows a converted policy to offer substantially similar benefits to the group policy if the benefit levels required in subdivision (9) of subsection 1 of section 376.397 exceed those provided under the group policy.

headings.title: Group insurance coverage election in lieu of individual
headings.reviewNote: Permits group insurers to provide continued group coverage in lieu of issuing separate individual converted policies.

headings.title: Out-of-state delivery on approved foreign policy forms
headings.reviewNote: Allows converted policies delivered outside Missouri to use forms authorized in the delivery jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires director approval for group accident and health policy forms, forty-five day review timelines, and regulatory exemptions.

headings.title: Mandatory director approval for group policy forms
headings.reviewNote: Bars delivering group accident or health insurance policies in Missouri without prior form approval by insurance director.

headings.title: Forty-five day review deadline and amendment notices
headings.reviewNote: Sets forty-five day deemed approval deadline, disapproval hearing rights, and thirty-day post-approval corrective amendments.

headings.title: Approval standards for unambiguous protective provisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires director to approve only clear, specific, unambiguous forms adequate to protect insured group members.

headings.title: Director exemption of specific forms by bulletin
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to exempt particular policy documents or forms from approval requirements by order or bulletin.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires family health benefit plans to cover newborns from birth including congenital defects, permits thirty-one day notice and premium conditions with a ten-day enrollment extension, with source notes recording ERISA preemption and case annotations.

headings.title: Immediate newborn infant coverage from birth moment
headings.reviewNote: Requires family health benefit plans to cover newly born children of enrollees immediately from the moment of birth.

headings.title: Scope of covered congenital defects and sickness
headings.reviewNote: Directs that newborn coverage includes injury, illness, and treatment of medically diagnosed congenital birth defects.

headings.title: Thirty-one day notification and ten-day extension
headings.reviewNote: Allows carriers to require notice and premium within thirty-one days, adding ten days if forms were requested.

headings.title: Applicability to policies issued after August 2001
headings.reviewNote: Applies the section to all health benefit plans delivered or issued for delivery in this state on or after August 28, 2001.

headings.title: Renewals and extensions deemed new policy issuances
headings.reviewNote: Provides that policy reviews, renewals, extensions, or premium alterations constitute new delivery for newborn rules.

headings.title: Definitions of health benefit plan and carrier
headings.reviewNote: Adopts statutory definitions of health benefit plan, health carrier, and enrollee from section 376.1350.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines 340B terms, bars manufacturers and third-party logistics providers from restricting 340B drug acquisition or delivery to contract pharmacies, treats violations as unlawful practices, and authorizes board of pharmacy complaint investigations and rulemaking.

headings.title: Definitions for 340B covered drug protections
headings.reviewNote: Defines 340B drug, covered entity, package, pharmaceutical manufacturer, pharmacy, and third-party logistics provider by reference to federal and state provisions.

headings.title: Prohibited manufacturer restrictions on 340B acquisitions
headings.reviewNote: Bars a pharmaceutical manufacturer, third-party logistics provider, or their agents or affiliates from denying, restricting, or prohibiting acquisition or delivery of a 340B drug to a contract pharmacy unless prohibited by the federal department, with wholesale distributors not treated as agents or affiliates.

headings.title: Violations deemed unlawful practices under section 407.020
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a prohibited act is an unlawful practice under section 407.020 with actions under sections 407.010 to 407.130 available, and treats each package as a separate violation.

headings.title: Board of pharmacy complaint investigations and discipline
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the state board of pharmacy to investigate complaints of subsection 2 violations by its licensees and to impose discipline, suspension, or revocation of the license.

headings.title: Board of pharmacy administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes state board of pharmacy to promulgate administrative rules to enforce 340B manufacturer prohibitions.

headings.title: Construction consistent with federal drug laws
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that section provisions shall not be construed or applied to be less restrictive than governing federal law.

headings.title: Limited REMS drug distribution plans permitted
headings.reviewNote: Provides that restricted drug distribution required under FDA risk evaluation and mitigation strategies is not a violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines 340B terms, bars health carriers and pharmacy benefits managers from discriminating against covered entities, requires civil penalties up to five thousand dollars per violation per day, and requires rules.

headings.title: Definitions of 340B entity, carrier, and PBM
headings.reviewNote: Defines 340B drug, covered entity, health carrier, and pharmacy benefits manager for discriminatory practice bans.

headings.title: Prohibited carrier and PBM discrimination against 340B entities
headings.reviewNote: Bars carriers, pharmacy benefits managers, and their agents or affiliates from discriminating against covered entities through lower reimbursement, differing terms or conditions, 340B-based reimbursement differences, 340B identification requirements, refusing to cover 340B drugs, or requiring claim reversal or resubmission.

headings.title: Mandatory civil penalty up to five thousand dollars per violation per day
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to impose a civil penalty not exceeding five thousand dollars per violation per day on a carrier, pharmacy benefits manager, or agent or affiliate that violates the section.

headings.title: Director required to promulgate implementing rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to promulgate rules implementing the section, effective only if compliant with chapter 536, with a nonseverability provision.

entries.reviewSummary: Enumerates authorized group health insurance categories, out-of-state policy rules, and authorized non-smoker employer premium discounts.

headings.title: Authorized categories for group health insurance policies
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates valid group types: employers, multi-employer trusts, labor unions, associations, credit unions, and debtor groups.

headings.title: Public interest findings for non-enumerated group policies
headings.reviewNote: Allows group health insurance for other groups only if the director finds issuance is not contrary to the public's best interest, would produce economies of acquisition or administration, and has benefits reasonable in relation to premiums, with out-of-state policy determinations and underwriting exclusions.

headings.title: Non-tobacco user premium discount authorization
headings.reviewNote: Permits health insurers to offer employer plans featuring premium discounts for non-smoking employees without unfair practice.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires written disclosure notices when compensation is paid to policyholders or sponsoring entities in direct response solicitations.

headings.title: Definitions of direct response solicitation and endorsing entity
headings.reviewNote: Defines direct response solicitation and sponsoring or endorsing entity communicating endorsement of insurance programs.

headings.title: Mandatory disclosure of compensation paid to sponsoring entity
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice on applications disclosing compensation paid directly or indirectly to endorsing group policyholders.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets qualifications for consultants reviewing denied chiropractic claims, bars percentage-based compensation, directs department investigation of complaints, addresses advertising and unlawful acceptance of employment, and authorizes board rules and fees.

headings.title: Mandatory qualifications for chiropractic claim review consultants
headings.reviewNote: Requires chiropractic reviewers to hold board certificates, 100 postgraduate training hours, and active clinical practice.

headings.title: Percentage-based reduction fee compensation prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits compensating chiropractic review consultants based on a percentage of claim payment reductions.

headings.title: Department investigation of unfair settlement practices
headings.reviewNote: Directs insurance director to investigate insured or chiropractor complaints alleging unfair chiropractic claim settlement.

headings.title: Misleading advertising by noncompliant claims consultants
headings.reviewNote: Deems public claims consulting advertising without board compliance to be false, misleading, and deceptive advertising.

headings.title: Unlawful practice and chiropractic board disciplinary action
headings.reviewNote: Makes uncertified claims consulting unlawful and authorizes disciplinary action by the board of chiropractic examiners.

headings.title: Chiropractic board certification rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes board of chiropractic examiners to establish rules and conditions for issuing consultant certificates.

headings.title: Fee setting authority for claims consulting certificates
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes board of chiropractic examiners to set certificate fees to cover administration expenses under chapter 331.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines terms and bars student accident policies from limiting or excluding surgical benefits to one procedure when multiple procedures are done in one operating session.

headings.title: Definitions for student accident policy section
headings.reviewNote: Defines institution of higher learning, sponsoring or endorsing entity, and student accident policy for purposes of the section.

headings.title: No one-procedure limit for multiple procedures in one session
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no student accident policy issued or delivered for issuance in this state shall limit or exclude surgical benefits to one procedure when multiple procedures are done in one operating session.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs assignment of health benefits to providers, direct payment instruments, prompt pay rules, and out-of-network exceptions.

headings.title: Definitions for assignment of insurance benefit payments
headings.reviewNote: Defines health benefit plan, health care services, health carrier, insured, insurer, and provider for purposes of the assignment of benefits section.

headings.title: Payment instrument in provider's name and thirty-day payment
headings.reviewNote: Requires an insurer, upon receipt of an assignment of benefits to a provider, to issue the payment instrument in the provider's name and pay claims within thirty days of receiving all documents reasonably needed to determine the claim.

headings.title: Voluntary single direct payment to health care providers
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that insurers are not precluded from voluntarily issuing reimbursement instruments payable solely to providers.

headings.title: Assignment rules not expanding out-of-network coverage terms
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that assignment provisions do not mandate payment to out-of-network providers when not covered under plan.

headings.title: Direct payment for authorized out-of-network services
headings.reviewNote: Requires direct payment to providers for all services when a plan does not require payment to out-of-network providers for most covered services and the carrier authorized services from a provider outside the network.

headings.title: Application of prompt payment interest and penalties
headings.reviewNote: Makes payments to providers under this section subject to section 376.383, with a delayed effective date of January 1, 2026 for entities not currently subject to that section.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires group health policies to provide continuation coverage in the same manner as federal COBRA, extends the privilege to spouses upon dissolution of marriage or death, addresses conversion rights, and limits application to persons not subject to federal continuation provisions.

headings.title: State group continuation mirroring federal COBRA standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires group policies insuring employees or members for hospital, surgical, or major medical coverage to allow continuation of coverage upon termination of employment or membership in the same manner as required under federal COBRA.

headings.title: Spousal continuation upon dissolution of marriage or death
headings.reviewNote: Gives the spouse of an employee or member whose coverage would otherwise end due to dissolution of marriage or death the same continuation privilege accorded the employee or member.

headings.title: Conversion rights following expiration of continuation period
headings.reviewNote: Provides individual converted policy rights under sections 376.395 to 376.404 upon conclusion of continuation period.

headings.title: Applies only to persons not subject to federal continuation provisions
headings.reviewNote: Limits the section to persons not subject to the continuation and conversion provisions of ERISA Title I, Subtitle B, Part 6 or Title XXII of the Public Health Service Act as in effect on January 1, 1987.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates health coverage for routine patient care costs in approved clinical trials, phase II/III/IV protocols, and informed consent.

headings.title: Mandatory coverage for approved cancer clinical trial care
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualifying health benefit plans on or after August 28, 2006 to cover routine patient care costs from phase II, III, or IV trials approved by listed entities for cancer prevention, early detection, or treatment, with phase II network limits allowed.

headings.title: Facility qualifications and personnel expertise requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires the treating facility and personnel to have the expertise, training, and patient volume to provide the treatment, with equal or superior noninvestigational alternatives and data giving a reasonable expectation of superiority.

headings.title: Routine costs for FDA-approved drugs and devices in trials
headings.reviewNote: Includes routine patient care costs for FDA-approved drugs and devices regardless of whether approved for the patient's condition, including reasonable and medically necessary services to administer the drug or device under evaluation.

headings.title: Applicability to phase III and IV government trials
headings.reviewNote: Applies routine care coverage to phase III or IV trials approved by NIH, FDA, VA, Defense, or institutional review boards.

headings.title: Applicability to phase II trials and enrolled patients
headings.reviewNote: Covers routine care for enrolled patients in phase II trials sanctioned by NIH or National Cancer Institute centers.

headings.title: Electronic posting of approved institutional review trials
headings.reviewNote: Requires entities seeking coverage under IRB trials to maintain and post detailed lists of qualifying clinical trials.

headings.title: Definitions of cooperative group and routine patient costs
headings.reviewNote: Defines cooperative group, multiple project assurance contract, and routine patient care costs excluding investigational drugs.

headings.title: Patient informed consent requirement and insurer access
headings.reviewNote: Requires providers participating in clinical trials to obtain patient informed consent consistent with current legal and ethical standards and make the documents available to the health insurer upon request.

headings.title: Exemption for Medicare and Medicaid government programs
headings.reviewNote: Exempts health plans and contracts funded under Title XVIII Medicare or Title XIX Medicaid from clinical trial rules.

headings.title: Exemption of supplemental and limited benefit policies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts accident-only, specified disease, hospital indemnity, Medicare supplement, and short-term plans from trial mandate.

headings.title: Phase II coverage an option for individually underwritten plans
headings.reviewNote: Provides that phase II clinical trial coverage does not apply automatically to individually underwritten health benefit plans but shall be an option to any such plan.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants public entity self-insurance health plans Medicaid third-party subrogation rights, remedies, and employee-paid policy exemptions.

headings.title: Subrogation and Medicaid remedies for public entities
headings.reviewNote: Grants public entity self-insured health plans the same third-party recovery rights and remedies as state Medicaid.

headings.title: Definition of public entity for self-insurance
headings.reviewNote: Defines public entity by statutory cross-reference to section 107.170 for self-insurance subrogation rules.

headings.title: Exemption for employee-funded supplemental policies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts limited benefit supplemental health insurance policies paid for entirely by public entity employees.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes carrier liability for claims incurred during policy grace periods and governs discontinuance notices to policyholders.

headings.title: Carrier liability for claims during grace periods
headings.reviewNote: Holds carriers liable for valid claims incurred during grace periods if premiums are received or stated in contract.

headings.title: Liability continuation pending written discontinuance notice
headings.reviewNote: Extends carrier claim liability beyond grace period if carrier actions treat policy as active prior to formal notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires carriers to provide three-year aggregated claims experience reports to employers with fifty-one or more covered lives.

headings.title: Three-year claims experience reporting on employer request
headings.reviewNote: Requires health carriers to provide three-year aggregated paid claim dollar reports to qualifying employers within thirty days.

headings.title: Employer eligibility criteria for claims reporting
headings.reviewNote: Limits reporting entitlement to employers with at least fifty-one covered lives insured continuously for twenty-two months.

headings.title: Definition of covered lives for reporting eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Defines covered lives as insured employees, spouses, and dependents under the group health benefit plan.

entries.reviewSummary: Prescribes carrier discontinuance notice contents, employer liability for collected contributions, and employee notice supplies.

headings.title: Discontinuance notice requests and employer liability warning
headings.reviewNote: Requires discontinuance notice to urge employee notification and warns employer of sole liability for collected contributions.

headings.title: Carrier duty to furnish employee discontinuance notices
headings.reviewNote: Directs health carrier to furnish supply of written notice forms for employer distribution to covered employees.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates extension of benefits for totally disabled employees upon group contract discontinuance, setting duration standards.

headings.title: Mandatory benefit extensions for total disability at discontinuance
headings.reviewNote: Requires group life, disability, and health policies to provide twelve-month or ninety-day benefit extensions for total disability.

headings.title: Certificate disclosures and regular benefit limit application
headings.reviewNote: Requires describing disability benefit extensions in certificates and allows application of regular contract limits.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires health carriers to provide timely enrollee cost-sharing estimates via internet or alternative means, exempting supplemental plans.

headings.title: Timely disclosure of enrollee cost-sharing responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires carriers to let individuals learn, in a timely manner on request, the cost-sharing they would pay for a specific item or service by a participating provider, available at minimum through an internet website and other means for individuals without internet access.

headings.title: Exemption of supplemental and limited benefit policies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts accident-only, specified disease, hospital indemnity, Medicare supplement, and short-term plans from cost disclosures.

headings.title: Effective date for enrollee cost-sharing disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that statutory cost-sharing disclosure requirements become effective on January 1, 2014.

entries.reviewSummary: Cites Missouri HIPAA and defines terms, and sets limits on preexisting condition exclusions, creditable coverage counting, certification, special enrollment periods, and health maintenance organization affiliation periods.

headings.title: Title cited as Missouri HIPAA and statutory definitions
headings.reviewNote: Cites Missouri Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and defines affiliation period, creditable coverage, and plans.

headings.title: Conditions for imposing a preexisting condition exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Allows an issuer of group coverage to impose a preexisting condition exclusion only for conditions treated within the six months before enrollment, for no more than twelve months (eighteen for late enrollees), reduced by creditable coverage.

headings.title: Counting creditable coverage and sixty-three day breaks
headings.reviewNote: Excludes creditable coverage separated by a sixty-three day gap, disregards waiting and affiliation periods in the gap, counts coverage without regard to specific benefits unless the issuer elects category-based counting with disclosure, and allows certifications as proof.

headings.title: Circumstances barring preexisting condition exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Bars exclusions for individuals covered within thirty-one days of birth, children covered within thirty days of adoption or placement, and pregnancy, with the birth and adoption protections ending after a sixty-three day gap in coverage.

headings.title: Issuer certification of creditable coverage
headings.reviewNote: Requires a group health insurance issuer to provide a certification of creditable coverage as required by Public Law 104-191 and its regulations.

headings.title: Special enrollment periods for loss of coverage and new dependents
headings.reviewNote: Requires special enrollment periods for eligible employees or dependents who lost other coverage (requesting within thirty days) and for dependents on marriage, birth, or adoption, with specified effective dates.

headings.title: Conditions for health maintenance organization affiliation periods
headings.reviewNote: Allows a health maintenance organization plan to impose an affiliation period only if no preexisting condition exclusion applies, it is uniform, does not exceed two months (three for late enrollees), begins on the enrollment date, and runs concurrently with any waiting period.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits group health eligibility discrimination based on health status factors and restricts discriminatory group premium rates.

headings.title: Eligibility discrimination based on health factors prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Bars group issuers from conditioning eligibility or enrollment on medical conditions, claims experience, genetics, or disability.

headings.title: Premium discrimination based on health status prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits charging individuals higher group premiums based on health status factors while permitting wellness discounts.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs guaranteed renewability in large group health markets, permitted nonrenewals, ninety-day product notices, and market exits.

headings.title: Guaranteed renewability in large group health market
headings.reviewNote: Requires health insurance issuers to renew large group coverage at the option of the plan sponsor.

headings.title: Permitted grounds for nonrenewal of large group coverage
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes nonrenewal for nonpayment, fraud, participation violations, contribution failures, market exit, or moved service area.

headings.title: Ninety-day notice for discontinuing specific group products
headings.reviewNote: Requires ninety days notice and uniform alternative product offers when discontinuing a particular large group coverage type.

headings.title: One hundred eighty-day notice and five-year market ban
headings.reviewNote: Mandates 180 days notice for complete market exit and bans re-entering Missouri large group market for five years.

headings.title: Uniform product modifications permitted at annual renewal
headings.reviewNote: Allows an issuer, at renewal, to modify coverage for a product offered to a large group health plan, with renewal deemed to occur not more often than annually unless a longer term is specified.

headings.title: Bona fide association employers treated as plan sponsors
headings.reviewNote: Provides that employer members of bona fide associations are deemed plan sponsors for guaranteed renewability provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires employers paying health premiums to establish federal Section 125 premium-only cafeteria plans, exempting self-funded plans.

headings.title: Mandatory Section 125 premium-only cafeteria plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires premium-paying employers to establish Section 125 cafeteria plans, exempting self-insured health plans.

headings.title: Employer choice of group coverage or defined contributions
headings.reviewNote: Preserves employer flexibility to provide traditional group plans or defined contribution cafeteria plans.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes guaranteed renewability in individual health markets, permitted discontinuations, five-year market bans, and modifications.

headings.title: Guaranteed renewability in individual health insurance market
headings.reviewNote: Requires health insurance issuers to renew individual coverage in force at the option of the covered individual.

headings.title: Permitted grounds for nonrenewal of individual policies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes nonrenewal for premium default, fraud, market withdrawal, departure from network service area, or association termination.

headings.title: Ninety-day notice for discontinuing individual policy types
headings.reviewNote: Requires ninety days advance notice and alternative policy purchase options when discontinuing a particular individual product.

headings.title: Complete market exit notice and five-year ban
headings.reviewNote: Requires 180 days notice to director and individuals for complete market withdrawal, barring re-entry for five years.

headings.title: Uniform policy form modifications permitted at renewal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes uniform modifications of individual policy forms at annual renewal consistent with state insurance law.

headings.title: Application to coverage sold through bona fide associations
headings.reviewNote: Provides that, where individual coverage is made available only through associations, a reference to an individual includes the association of which the individual is a member.

headings.title: Insurer certification of creditable coverage
headings.reviewNote: Requires an insurer to provide a certification of creditable coverage as required by Public Law 104-191 and its regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Cites the Missouri Health Insurance Rate Transparency Act, defines terms, requires rate filings with timing rules for use, directs public comment and reasonableness determinations, provides publication and rulemaking provisions, and sets applicability.

headings.title: Title cited as Health Insurance Rate Transparency Act
headings.reviewNote: Cites section as the Missouri Health Insurance Rate Transparency Act.

headings.title: Legislative intent regarding transparent rate reviews
headings.reviewNote: States legislative intent to promote transparency and accountability in health insurance premium rate determinations.

headings.title: Statutory definitions for health rate transparency provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines director, excepted health benefit plan, grandfathered health benefit plan, health benefit plan, health carrier, individual market, and small group market for purposes of the section.

headings.title: Prior rate filing prerequisite for delivering health plans
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits delivering or renewing health benefit plans until premium rates are filed with the insurance department.

headings.title: Thirty-day informational rate filings for excepted plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires excepted health benefit plan rates to be filed thirty days before use for informational purposes only, and provides that rates shall not be excessive, inadequate, or unfairly discriminatory.

headings.title: Thirty-day informational rate filings for grandfathered plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires thirty-day advance informational rate filings for grandfathered group and individual health benefit plans.

headings.title: Rate use timing and sufficiency of filing documentation
headings.reviewNote: Allows a carrier to use rates for non-grandfathered, non-excepted plans on the earliest of the director's reasonableness determination, notice of intent to use rates deemed unreasonable, or sixty days after filing, and lets the director notify the carrier within sixty days of insufficient documentation.

headings.title: Rate filings in form and content prescribed by rule
headings.reviewNote: Requires proposed rates and rate filing documentation to be submitted in the form and content prescribed by rule, consistent with 45 CFR 154 and including review standards consistent with it.

headings.title: Public availability timing and trade secret protection
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to determine by rule when filed rates are publicly available, and provides that rate filing documentation designated by the carrier as trade secret or proprietary is not a public record.

headings.title: Sixty-day review and reasonableness determination by director
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to provide a means for public comment, review rate filings, determine whether a rate is unreasonable under 45 CFR 154, and give written notice of the determination within sixty days after submission.

headings.title: Carrier options within thirty days of unreasonable-rate notice
headings.reviewNote: Allows a carrier, within thirty days after written notice that proposed rates are unreasonable, to amend its rates, request reconsideration based on additional information, or implement the proposed rates, and requires notifying the director of its intention within that period.

headings.title: Department public notice of implemented unreasonable rates
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to make a determination public, in a form and manner set by rule, if a carrier implements a rate the director determined to be unreasonable.

headings.title: Department website publication of final approved rates
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to publish final rates on the department's website no earlier than thirty days before the first day of the individual market's annual open enrollment period for the applicable calendar year.

headings.title: Mutual extension of statutory rate review timeframes
headings.reviewNote: Allows the time frames described in the section to be extended upon mutual agreement between the director and the health carrier.

headings.title: Director administrative rulemaking authority for rate transparency
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to promulgate administrative rules to implement rate transparency and filing procedures.

headings.title: Applicability date and initial implementation rules
headings.reviewNote: Applies the section to health benefit plans delivered, issued, continued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2018, and requires the director to promulgate initial implementation rules effective no later than March 1, 2017.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits life insurers from denying applications or charging differential premiums based on past lawful travel, deeming it unfair practice.

headings.title: Discrimination based on past lawful travel prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Bars life insurers from denying applications, refusing to renew, cancelling, restricting, terminating, or charging a different rate based on past or future lawful travel destinations, except where based on sound actuarial principles or actual or reasonably anticipated experience.

headings.title: Travel discrimination classified as unfair trade practice
headings.reviewNote: Classifies life insurance travel discrimination as an unfair trade practice subject to chapter 375 sanctions.

headings.title: Applicability to life policies issued or renewed after August 2009
headings.reviewNote: Applies the section to any life insurance policy issued or renewed on or after August 28, 2009.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires insured consent for life policies, establishes employer insurable interest in employees, and sets welfare liability caps.

headings.title: Insured written consent requirement and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires the competent insured's application or written consent for individual life contracts (except group life), with exceptions for insurance on minors by persons with insurable interest or support responsibility and for family policies.

headings.title: Employer insurable interest in employees and negative consent
headings.reviewNote: Establishes employer insurable interest in employees, allowing coverage with thirty-day negative consent notice.

headings.title: Benefit limitations matching aggregate welfare plan liabilities
headings.reviewNote: Limits the employer's or trust's insurable interest in nonmanagement and retired employees to aggregate projected death benefits commensurate with aggregate projected liabilities under employee welfare benefit plans, calculated on generally accepted actuarial principles.

headings.title: Definition of employer and controlled corporate affiliates
headings.reviewNote: Defines employer broadly under Internal Revenue Code control principles using fifty-one percent ownership threshold.

headings.title: Preservation of other common law insurable interests
headings.reviewNote: Provides that statutory employer rules do not restrict other valid common law or statutory insurable interests.

headings.title: Insurable interest determined at policy effective date
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that insurable interest is determined at contract inception and need not persist at time of death loss.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits misrepresentations and misleading circulars in life insurance sales and bars discounting premium notes prior to delivery.

headings.title: Misleading circulars, false estimates, and misrepresentations prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits life companies and agents from circulating misleading illustrations, misrepresenting terms, or misnaming policy types.

headings.title: Soliciting agent status and restriction on premium notes
headings.reviewNote: Deems soliciting person agent of insurer and bars discounting premium notes prior to personal delivery of policy.

entries.reviewSummary: Permits one-year suicide liability exclusions in life policies and mandates prompt refund of all premiums paid upon suicide.

headings.title: One-year suicide exclusion in life policies permitted
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes excluding suicide liability within one year of policy issuance or death benefit increases.

headings.title: Mandatory prompt refund of paid policy premiums
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers to promptly refund all premiums paid for excluded coverage if insured dies by suicide within one year.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets annuity contract nonforfeiture requirements, including exemptions, required paid-up and cash surrender provisions, minimum nonforfeiture amount calculation, benefit calculation rules, disclosures, and operative dates.

headings.title: Exemptions from annuity nonforfeiture statutory requirements
headings.reviewNote: Exempts reinsurance, group annuities under employer plans, variable annuities, immediate annuities, and out-of-state contracts.

headings.title: Mandatory paid-up annuity and cash surrender provisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires annuity contracts to provide paid-up benefits upon cessation of payments and cash surrender options.

headings.title: Computation of minimum nonforfeiture values for annuities
headings.reviewNote: Establishes computation formulas for net considerations and minimum nonforfeiture interest rates based on treasury yields.

headings.title: Calculation of present value of paid-up annuity benefits
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that paid-up annuity benefits must equal the present value of minimum nonforfeiture amounts at maturity.

headings.title: Cash surrender benefit minimums before maturity
headings.reviewNote: Requires cash surrender benefits prior to maturity to be not less than the present value of the paid-up maturity benefit (adjusted for withdrawals, loans, and credits) and not less than the minimum nonforfeiture amount, with a death benefit at least equal to the cash surrender benefit.

headings.title: Paid-up annuity value where no cash surrender benefit
headings.reviewNote: For contracts without cash surrender benefits, requires the present value of a paid-up annuity nonforfeiture option before maturity to be not less than the present value of the maturity paid-up benefit and not less than the minimum nonforfeiture amount.

headings.title: Maturity date deemed for optional maturity dates
headings.reviewNote: For benefit calculations under subsections 5 and 6, deems the maturity date to be the latest date the contract permits, but not later than the anniversary after the annuitant's seventieth birthday or the tenth anniversary, whichever is later.

headings.title: Prominent statement when benefits are not provided
headings.reviewNote: Requires a contract that lacks cash surrender benefits or death benefits at least equal to the minimum nonforfeiture amount before annuity payments to state in a prominent place that such benefits are not provided.

headings.title: Benefits calculated with allowance for time lapse
headings.reviewNote: Requires paid-up annuity, cash surrender, or death benefits available at times other than the contract anniversary under fixed scheduled consideration contracts to be calculated with allowance for the lapse of time and scheduled considerations.

headings.title: Contracts combining annuity and life insurance benefits
headings.reviewNote: Requires contracts combining annuity and excess life insurance benefits to compute minimum nonforfeiture benefits as the sum for each portion as if separate, and disregards additional disability or reversionary benefits in computing the minimum amounts.

headings.title: Optional election and operative date of July 1, 2006
headings.reviewNote: Allows a company to elect, form by form before July 1, 2006, to apply this section in lieu of section 376.671, and otherwise makes the section operative for contracts issued after July 1, 2006 (source note records effective dates of 6-21-04 and 8-28-04).

entries.reviewSummary: Sets standard nonforfeiture provisions for life insurance policies, including required paid-up and cash surrender provisions, adjusted premium and mortality table rules, nonforfeiture interest rates, exclusions, and company operative date elections.

headings.title: Meaning of operative date of the valuation manual
headings.reviewNote: Provides that 'operative date of the valuation manual' has the same meaning as in section 376.365.

headings.title: Mandatory paid-up nonforfeiture and cash surrender provisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires life policies issued on or after the operative date to contain, in substance, paid-up nonforfeiture benefit on default (request within sixty days), cash surrender value after three (ordinary) or five (industrial) years, election, and calculation statements, or provisions at least as favorable.

headings.title: Inapplicable provisions may be omitted from the policy
headings.reviewNote: Allows provisions inapplicable by reason of the plan of insurance to be omitted from the policy to the extent inapplicable.

headings.title: Company may defer cash surrender payment six months
headings.reviewNote: Reserves to the company the right to defer payment of any cash surrender value for six months after demand with surrender of the policy.

headings.title: Minimum cash surrender values on default and after paid-up
headings.reviewNote: Sets minimum cash surrender values on default or when paid up, based on present value of future guaranteed benefits less adjusted premiums and indebtedness, with adjustments for supplemental benefit riders and family policies.

headings.title: Paid-up nonforfeiture benefit present value minimum
headings.reviewNote: Requires a paid-up nonforfeiture benefit on default to have a present value at least equal to the cash surrender value provided or that would be required in the absence of a minimum premium-payment period.

headings.title: Adjusted premium calculation for earlier policies
headings.reviewNote: Sets adjusted premium calculation as a uniform percentage of policy premiums for policies issued before the subsection 14 operative date, including present value of guaranteed benefits, two percent of insurance, and first-year percentages.

headings.title: Four percent cap on adjusted premium and issue date definition
headings.reviewNote: Limits adjusted premiums to four percent of the amount of insurance when applying subsection 7 percentages and defines the date of issue as the date the insured's rated age is determined.

headings.title: Equivalent uniform amount for varying amounts of insurance
headings.reviewNote: Defines the equivalent uniform amount for policies providing varying amounts of insurance, with a special rule for policies on children under age ten.

headings.title: Adjusted premiums for term insurance riders
headings.reviewNote: Sets adjusted premiums for policies with term insurance riders as the adjusted premium without the rider plus the adjusted premium for the term insurance, calculated separately.

headings.title: 1941 mortality tables and interest limit for earlier calculations
headings.reviewNote: Requires calculations for ordinary insurance on the Commissioners 1941 Standard Ordinary Mortality Table and industrial insurance on the 1941 Standard Industrial table, with interest not exceeding three and one-half percent (source note: word 'and' appears in original rolls).

headings.title: Commissioners 1958 table basis for ordinary policies
headings.reviewNote: Sets calculations for ordinary policies on the Commissioners 1958 Standard Ordinary Mortality Table with specified interest limits, female age setback, and company election of the operative date (January 1, 1966 absent election).

headings.title: Commissioners 1961 table basis for industrial policies
headings.reviewNote: Sets calculations for industrial policies on the Commissioners 1961 Standard Industrial Mortality Table with specified interest limits and company election of the operative date (January 1, 1968 absent election).

headings.title: Adjusted premium method, mortality tables, and nonforfeiture interest rate
headings.reviewNote: Sets the adjusted premium method with nonforfeiture net level premium, recalculation upon benefit changes, 1980 and 1961 mortality tables, valuation-manual provisions, nonforfeiture interest rate, refiling limits, and company election of operative date (January 1, 1989 absent election).

headings.title: Director approval for plans with undeterminable minimum values
headings.reviewNote: Requires, for plans with future premium determination or minimum values not determinable by subsections 1 to 14, that the director be satisfied benefits are substantially as favorable and not misleading and that values follow regulations.

headings.title: Values for defaults between anniversaries and paid-up additions
headings.reviewNote: Requires values for defaults other than on anniversaries to allow for lapse of time and fractional premiums, permits assuming death benefits are paid at policy year end, and sets a floor for the net value of paid-up additions.

headings.title: Additional benefits disregarded in nonforfeiture values
headings.reviewNote: Provides that accidental death, disability, reversionary annuity, certain term, child term, and other additional benefits and their premiums are disregarded in ascertaining required cash surrender and nonforfeiture benefits.

headings.title: Basic cash value and nonforfeiture factors for 1986 policies
headings.reviewNote: Applies to policies issued on or after January 1, 1986, limiting differences in cash surrender value from the basic cash value, defining nonforfeiture factors, and aligning mortality and interest bases and other values.

headings.title: Policies and benefits to which the section does not apply
headings.reviewNote: Exempts reinsurance, group insurance, pure endowments, annuities, specified term policies, low-value policies, and policies delivered outside this state, and sets the expiration age for joint term policies.

headings.title: Company election of operative date of the section
headings.reviewNote: Allows a company to file notice electing a specified operative date before January 1, 1948, with January 1, 1948 as the operative date absent election.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs nonforfeiture requirements for annuity contracts issued prior to July 2006, cash surrender calculations, and maturity rules.

headings.title: Exemptions from legacy annuity nonforfeiture standards
headings.reviewNote: Exempts reinsurance, group employer annuities, variable annuities, immediate annuities, and out-of-state contracts.

headings.title: Mandatory paid-up annuity and cash surrender contract provisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires contracts to provide paid-up annuity benefits upon cessation of considerations and cash surrender options.

headings.title: Computation of minimum nonforfeiture amounts for legacy annuities
headings.reviewNote: Defines minimum nonforfeiture amounts as accumulations of percentages of net considerations (flexible, fixed scheduled, or single) at three percent interest less withdrawals and indebtedness, with one and one-half percent for contracts issued July 1, 2002 to July 1, 2006.

headings.title: Calculation of present value of paid-up annuity benefits
headings.reviewNote: Requires paid-up annuity benefits to equal the present value of minimum nonforfeiture amounts at maturity.

headings.title: Calculation of cash surrender benefits before contract maturity
headings.reviewNote: Requires cash surrender benefits before maturity to be not less than the present value of the paid-up maturity benefit (adjusted for withdrawals, loans, and credits) and not less than the minimum nonforfeiture amount, with a death benefit at least equal to the cash surrender benefit.

headings.title: Paid-up annuity value where no cash surrender benefit
headings.reviewNote: For contracts without cash surrender benefits, requires the present value of a paid-up annuity nonforfeiture option before maturity to be not less than the present value of the maturity paid-up benefit and not less than the minimum nonforfeiture amount.

headings.title: Maturity date deemed for optional maturity dates
headings.reviewNote: For benefit calculations under subsections 5 and 6, deems the maturity date to be the latest date the contract permits, but not later than the anniversary after the annuitant's seventieth birthday or the tenth anniversary, whichever is later.

headings.title: Prominent statement when benefits are not provided
headings.reviewNote: Requires a contract that lacks cash surrender benefits or death benefits at least equal to the minimum nonforfeiture amount before annuity payments to state in a prominent place that such benefits are not provided.

headings.title: Benefits calculated with allowance for time lapse
headings.reviewNote: Requires paid-up annuity, cash surrender, or death benefits available at times other than the contract anniversary under fixed scheduled consideration contracts to be calculated with allowance for the lapse of time and scheduled considerations.

headings.title: Combined contracts providing both annuity and life insurance
headings.reviewNote: Requires contracts combining annuity and excess life insurance benefits to compute minimum nonforfeiture benefits as the sum for each portion as if separate, and disregards additional disability or reversionary benefits in computing the minimum amounts.

headings.title: Company election of operative date before September 28, 1981
headings.reviewNote: Allows a company, after September 28, 1979, to file notice electing a specified operative date before September 28, 1981, with September 28, 1981 as the operative date absent election.

headings.title: Section not applicable to new contracts after July 1, 2006
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the provisions of the section do not apply to any new contract entered into after July 1, 2006.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits discriminatory surplus sharing representations and regulates pure endowment benefits and coupon policy sales.

headings.title: Discriminatory earnings and preferential surplus claims prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Bars life policies and sales materials from promising discriminatory surplus sharing or preferential benefits to buyers.

headings.title: Regulations governing pure endowment benefits and coupons
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits coupon passbooks, requires fixed maturity dollar amounts, and bans competitive twisting claims regarding law.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes life policies without cash surrender values, requiring prominent first-page disclosures and comparative policy summaries.

headings.title: Life policies without cash surrender values authorized
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes life policies without cash surrender value, requiring prominent front-page disclosures and cost comparison summaries.

headings.title: Application of nonforfeiture provisions to surrender-free policies
headings.reviewNote: Applies nonforfeiture standards to policies without cash value except for payment upon surrender requirements.

headings.title: Inapplicability of statutory policy loan provisions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts policies lacking cash surrender values from statutory provisions governing policy loans.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires director approval for life policies and annuities, forty-five day reviews, hearing rights, and regulatory exemptions.

headings.title: Mandatory director approval for life policies and annuities
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits delivery of life insurance policies or annuity contracts without prior filing and approval by the insurance director.

headings.title: Forty-five day review period and deemed approval rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs insurance director to approve or disapprove policy forms within forty-five days, after which forms are deemed approved.

headings.title: Statutory standards for policy form approval and appeals
headings.reviewNote: Requires forms to be unambiguous, specific, and protective of insureds, providing written reasons and hearing rights.

headings.title: Director exemption of specific forms by bulletin
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to exempt particular life or annuity policy documents from approval requirements by order or bulletin.

entries.reviewSummary: Allows companies to issue life policies without cash surrender value before death, with first-page notice and prior policy summary requirements, nonforfeiture provisions applicable except surrender payment, and policy loan laws not applying.

headings.title: Life policies without cash surrender value authorized
headings.reviewNote: Allows a company, after September 28, 1987, to issue life policies differing from filed policies only by lacking cash surrender value before death, with first-page contrasting-type notice and a policy summary delivered before any premium is accepted.

headings.title: Nonforfeiture provisions apply except payment on surrender
headings.reviewNote: Provides that, except for payment upon surrender, nonforfeiture amounts for such policies are subject to chapter 376 provisions applying to cash surrender values of otherwise similar policies.

headings.title: Policy loan laws do not apply to such policies
headings.reviewNote: Provides that insurance laws relating to policy loans do not apply to policies that do not provide cash surrender values.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires life insurers to furnish annual policy statements and provide detailed policy values and loans upon holder request.

headings.title: Mandatory annual statement to life policyholders and annuitants
headings.reviewNote: Requires life insurers to provide annual identification notices to whole life and deferred annuity holders showing premiums due.

headings.title: Duty to furnish policy values upon holder request
headings.reviewNote: Directs insurers to furnish plan types, insurance amounts, policy values, loans, and dividends within reasonable time upon request.

entries.reviewSummary: Bars insurers from setting fees on noncovered optometric services, prohibits de minimis reimbursements, and protects supplier choice.

headings.title: Insurer fee limits on noncovered optometric care prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits vision and health plans from limiting optometrist fees for services or materials unless reimbursed as covered care.

headings.title: Customary rate limits for noncovered optometric care
headings.reviewNote: Bars vision providers from charging more than usual and customary rates for noncovered services or materials.

headings.title: Reasonable reimbursement required and de minimis evasion prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Requires plans to pay reasonable reimbursement and prohibits nominal or de minimis payments to evade section rules.

headings.title: Restricting patient supplier choice for materials prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Bars vision insurance policies and discount plans from restricting patient choice of material sources and suppliers.

headings.title: Optometrist contractual opt-in to discount plans
headings.reviewNote: Permits optometrists to contractually opt in to voluntary discount programs offered by vision and health carriers.

headings.title: Definitions for optometric service and vision plan rules
headings.reviewNote: Defines covered services, health benefit plan, health carrier, materials, optometric services, and vision plans.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates unanticipated out-of-network care claims, forty-five day offers, sixty-day negotiations, external arbitration, and surprise billing.

headings.title: Definitions for unanticipated out-of-network emergency care
headings.reviewNote: Defines emergency medical condition, facility, health care professional, carrier, and unanticipated out-of-network care.

headings.title: Claim submission, negotiation timelines, and balance billing ban
headings.reviewNote: Sets 180-day claim filing, 45-day payment offer, 60-day negotiation, arbitration referrals, and prohibits patient balance billing.

headings.title: Enrollee cost-sharing based on in-network terms
headings.reviewNote: Limits patient liability for surprise medical bills to in-network deductible, copayment, and out-of-pocket maximum terms.

headings.title: External arbitration process for disputed provider reimbursements
headings.reviewNote: Directs insurance director to ensure accessible binding external arbitration for unresolved out-of-network provider claims.

headings.title: Binding arbitration decision and closed record
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the arbitrator's final decision is binding on all parties, is copied to the director, and with the request and related documents is a closed record under section 374.071, and is not an agency decision or contested case.

headings.title: Arbitrator-determined amount between Medicare multiple and percentile
headings.reviewNote: Requires the arbitrator to determine a dollar amount between one hundred twenty percent of the Medicare-allowed amount and the seventieth percentile of the usual and customary rate, using benchmarks from independent nonprofit organizations.

headings.title: Factors the arbitrator shall consider in determining reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the arbitrator to consider listed factors (training and experience, nature of service, usual charge, circumstances and complexity, and average contracted rate) if the professional believes the offered payment does not recognize them.

headings.title: Enrollee participation not required and nondisclosure agreement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the enrollee is not required to participate in arbitration and requires the health care professional and carrier to execute a nondisclosure agreement before arbitration.

headings.title: Department rules and fees with nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Allows the department to promulgate rules and fees to implement the section, including arbitration procedures, effective only if compliant with chapter 536, with a nonseverability provision.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines direct response solicitations and requires written disclosures when compensation is paid to group life policyholders.

headings.title: Definitions of direct response solicitation and endorsing entity
headings.reviewNote: Defines direct response solicitation and endorsing entity communicating endorsement of group life insurance programs.

headings.title: Mandatory written notice of compensation to sponsoring entities
headings.reviewNote: Requires written disclosures to prospective insureds when compensation is paid to group policyholders or endorsers.

headings.title: Disclosure of direct or indirect third-party compensation
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice regardless of whether compensation is paid directly or directed to third parties or corporate affiliates.

headings.title: Placement of compensation notice on enrollment forms
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that compensation disclosure notices accompany or be placed directly on insurance applications or enrollment forms.

entries.reviewSummary: States legislative purpose to improve buyer understanding and cost comparison of life insurance, permitting additional sales materials.

headings.title: Purpose to improve life insurance buyer comprehension
headings.reviewNote: States statutory purpose to assist life insurance purchasers in selecting suitable plans and evaluating relative policy costs.

headings.title: Use of additional lawful sales materials permitted
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that life disclosure statutes do not prohibit using supplementary sales material that complies with state law.

entries.reviewSummary: Applies life solicitation disclosure rules to all issuers including fraternals, while exempting annuities, group, and variable life.

headings.title: Application of life disclosure laws to solicitations
